4.4.
Monad presentations of perverse coherent extensions

In this section, we generalize the construction of Section
3.4
, and its generalization in Section
3.5
, describing certain canonical resolutions of compactly supported perverse coherent sheaves in terms of representations of quivers, to describe objects of the category
\textup{Filt}(F\oplus M)
in terms of representations of extended quivers.

The compositions of the equivalences of Equations
4.11
and
4.12
define triangle equivalences

\hat{K}_{M}(\cdot):{\textup{D}}_{\textup{Perf}}(\Sigma_{M})\xrightarrow{\cong}\textup{Thick}(F\oplus M)\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad K_{M}(\cdot):{\textup{D}}_{\textup{perf}}(\Sigma_{M})\xrightarrow{\cong}\textup{thick}(F\oplus M)\ ,

analogous to the functors of Equations
3.17
and
3.18
. Our goal is to give an explicit presentation of the subcategory
\textup{PervCoh}_{M}(\hat{Y})
as the image of the corresponding subcategory
H^{0}(\textup{Tw}^{0}\mathcal{A}_{F\oplus M})
, and thus in terms of representations of the extended quiver
Q_{M}
.

One of the primary implications of commutativity in the statement of Theorem
4.18
is the following:

Corollary 4.23
.

There are canonical natural isomorphisms

(4.21)

\displaystyle\hat{K}_{M}\cong\hat{K}\circ(\cdot)^{N}\circ(\cdot)\otimes_{S_{M}}S

\displaystyle:{\textup{D}}_{\textup{Perf}}(\Sigma_{M})\to{\textup{D}}^{b}\textup{Coh}(\hat{Y})

and

(4.22)

\displaystyle K_{M}\cong K\circ(\cdot)^{N}\circ(\cdot)\otimes_{S_{M}}S

\displaystyle:{\textup{D}}_{\textup{perf}}(\Sigma_{M})\to{\textup{D}}^{b}\textup{Coh}(Y)^{T}

,

where
\hat{K}
and
K
are the functors of Equations
3.17
and
3.18
.

Proof.

These natural isomorphisms are simply the commutativity data for the outer squares of Equations
4.11
and
4.12
.
∎

Further, the preceding corollary induces the following equivalent presentations of these categories:

Corollary 4.24
.

The image of
{\textup{D}}_{\textup{perf}}(\Sigma_{M})
under
(\cdot)\otimes_{S_{M}}S:{\textup{D}}_{\textup{fr}}(\Sigma_{M})\to{\textup{D}}_{\textup{fd}}(\Sigma)
is given by

{\textup{D}}_{\textup{perf}}(\Sigma_{M})\xrightarrow{\cong}\textup{thick}(\Sigma\oplus\Hom(F,M))\subset{\textup{D}}_{\textup{fd}}(\Sigma)\ ,

inducing an equivalence of mixed categories between the corresponding subcategories

H^{0}(\textup{tw}^{0}(\mathcal{A}_{F\oplus M}))\xrightarrow{\cong}\textup{filt}_{\Sigma}(\Sigma\oplus\Hom(F,M))\ .

Similarly, image of
{\textup{D}}_{\textup{Perf}}(\Sigma_{M})
under
(\cdot)\otimes_{S_{M}}S:{\textup{D}}_{\textup{Fr}}(\Sigma_{M})\to{\textup{D}}_{\textup{Fd}}(\Sigma)
is given by

{\textup{D}}_{\textup{Perf}}(\Sigma_{M})\xrightarrow{\cong}\textup{Thick}(\Sigma\oplus\Hom(F,M))\subset{\textup{D}}_{\textup{Fd}}(\Sigma)\ ,

inducing an equivalence

H^{0}(\textup{Tw}^{0}(\mathcal{A}_{F\oplus M}))\xrightarrow{\cong}\textup{Filt}_{\Sigma}(\Sigma\oplus\Hom(F,M))\ .

Proof.

This follows immediately, noting that the image of
\Sigma_{M}
is given by

\Sigma_{M}\otimes_{S_{M}}S=\Hom(F\oplus M,F\oplus M)\otimes_{S_{M}}S\cong\Hom(F,F\oplus M)=\Sigma\oplus\Hom(F,M)\ .

∎

Thus, it remains to understand the image of (the Nakayama dual of)
\textup{filt}_{\Sigma}(\Sigma\oplus\Hom(F,M))
under the functor
K:{\textup{D}}_{\textup{perf}}(\Sigma)\to{\textup{D}}^{b}\textup{Coh}(Y)^{T}
studied in Section
3.4
, generalizing the calculation of the image of
\textup{filt}_{\Sigma}(\Sigma)
in
loc. cit.
(as well as its I-adically complete, ungraded variant).

Warning 4.25
.

For concreteness, we give most of the exposition in this section in the graded case, noting the ungraded variant can be recovered by completing and forgetting the grading. Further, for notation simplicity we will restrict the trigrading along a cocharacter
{\mathbb{C}}^{\times}\to T
, in keeping with Warning
3.14
.

To begin, we let

\Sigma_{\infty}=\Hom(F,M),\ I_{\infty}=\Hom(F,M)^{N}\ \in{\textup{D}}_{\textup{fd}}(\Sigma)

and similarly for
\Sigma_{\infty},I_{\infty}\in{\textup{D}}_{\textup{Fd}}(\Sigma)
, and suppose
I_{\infty}
has Jordan-Holder series

(4.23)

I_{\infty}=[I_{\infty}^{0}<I_{\infty}^{-1}\langle 1\rangle<\cdots<I_{\infty}^{-m_{\infty}}\langle m_{\infty}\rangle]\ ,

in the cohomologically sheared notation, in analogy with Equation
3.22
. Then the image of
I_{\infty}
under the explicit presentation of the Koszul duality functor established in Section
3.4
is given by

K(I_{\infty})=\left[I_{i}^{-m_{\infty}}\otimes_{S}E[m_{\infty}]\to\cdots\to I_{\infty}^{-1}\otimes_{S}E[1]\to I_{\infty}^{0}\otimes_{S}E\right]\xrightarrow{\cong}M\ ,

as in Equation
3.23
. Further, we have canonical identifications

(4.24)

\ {}_{\infty}(\Sigma_{M})_{i}^{1}

\displaystyle\cong\Hom_{\Sigma}(I_{\infty},I_{i}\langle 1\rangle)\cong\Hom^{0}_{{\textup{D}}^{b}\textup{Coh}(Y)}(K(I_{\infty}),K(I_{i})[1])

(4.25)

\ {}_{i}(\Sigma_{M})_{\infty}^{1}

\displaystyle\cong\Hom_{\Sigma}(I_{i},I_{\infty}\langle 1\rangle)\cong\Hom^{0}_{{\textup{D}}^{b}\textup{Coh}(Y)}(K(I_{i}),K(I_{\infty})[1])

(4.26)

\ {}_{\infty}(\Sigma_{M})_{\infty}^{1}

\displaystyle\cong\Hom_{\Sigma}(I_{\infty},I_{\infty}\langle 1\rangle)\cong\Hom^{0}_{{\textup{D}}^{b}\textup{Coh}(Y)}(K(I_{\infty}),K(I_{\infty})[1])

as in Equation
3.24
, though we note that
I_{\infty}\in{\textup{D}}_{\textup{fd}}(\Sigma)
is not necessarily injective so the
\Hom
functors over
\Sigma
appearing in the preceding equations are not necessarily exact, in contrast to those in
loc. cit.
.

Given an object
(i_{1},...,i_{d},\delta)\in\textup{tw}^{0}\mathcal{A}_{F\oplus M}
, where we recall that each
i_{k}\in I_{M}=I\cup\{\infty\}
, the corresponding object of
{\textup{D}}_{\textup{fd}}(\Sigma)
has underlying bigraded vector space given by

\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}}=\bigoplus_{k=1,...,d}\Sigma_{i_{k}}\langle p_{k}\rangle\cong\bigoplus_{i\in I_{M}}\Sigma_{i}\otimes V_{i}\cong\left(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\Sigma_{i}\otimes V_{i}\right)\oplus(\Sigma_{\infty}\otimes V_{\infty})

where each
V_{i}
is a graded vector space

V_{i}=\bigoplus_{p\in\mathbb{Z}}V_{i,-p}\langle p\rangle\quad\quad\text{with}\quad\quad\dim V_{i,p}=\#\{k\in\{1,...,d\}\ |\ i_{k}=i\textup{ and }p_{k}=p\}\ .

Note in particular that
\dim\oplus_{i\in I_{M}}V_{i}=d
.

Now, the degree zero element
\delta\in\mathfrak{gl}_{d}(\mathbb{Z}\mathcal{A}_{F\oplus M})[1]
is in fact an element of the subspace

\delta\in\Hom_{{\textup{D}}(\Sigma_{M})}(\bigoplus_{i\in I_{M}}(\Sigma_{M})_{i}\otimes V_{i},\bigoplus_{j\in I_{M}}(\Sigma_{M})_{j}\otimes V_{j}[1])\subset\mathfrak{gl}_{d}(\Sigma_{M})[1]\cong\mathfrak{gl}_{d}(\mathcal{A}_{F\oplus M})[1]

and thus admits a decomposition

(4.27)

\delta=\sum_{i,j\in I_{M}}b_{ij}\otimes B_{ij}\quad\in\quad\bigoplus_{i,j\in I_{M}}\ {}_{i}(\Sigma_{M})_{j}\otimes\Hom(V_{i},V_{j})[1]\ ,

as in Equation
3.31
, where we again use the abuse of notation
B_{ij}\otimes b_{ij}
to denote a not necessarily pure tensor, as in Warning
3.25
.

The underlying cochain complex differential is given by

d_{\delta}=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\rho_{k}^{\Sigma\oplus\Sigma_{\infty}}(\cdot,\delta^{\otimes k-1})\quad\in\quad\Hom_{{\textup{D}}(\Sigma)}(\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}},\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}}[1])

where
\rho_{k}^{\Sigma\oplus\Sigma_{\infty}}:\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}}\otimes\Sigma_{M}^{\otimes k-1}\to\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}}[1-k]
denote the image under
(\cdot)\otimes_{S_{M}}S
of the
A_{\infty}
module structure maps for
(\Sigma_{M})_{i_{1},...,i_{s}}
over
\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{A}_{F\oplus M}}
. Decomposing according to Equation
4.27
, we have the analogous decomposition

(4.28)

d_{\delta}=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z},\ i,i_{2},...,i_{k-1},j\in I_{M}}\rho_{k}^{\Sigma\oplus\Sigma_{\infty}}(\cdot,b_{ii_{2}},...,b_{i_{k-1}j})\otimes(B_{ii_{2}}...B_{i_{k-1}j})\quad\in\quad\bigoplus_{i,j\in I_{M}}\Hom(\Sigma_{i},\Sigma_{j}[1])\otimes\Hom(V_{i},V_{j})\

of the differential on
\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}}^{\delta}
.

Thus, the image of the Nakayama dual of
\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}}^{\delta}\in{\textup{D}_{\textup{perf}}}(\Sigma)
under the Koszul duality equivalence of Equation
3.18
is given by

(4.29)

K(\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}}^{\delta,N})=\left(K(\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}}^{N}),K(d_{\delta}^{N})\right)\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad K(\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}}^{N})=\bigoplus_{i\in I_{M}}K(I_{i})\otimes V_{i}\ ,

and where the differential
K(d_{\delta}^{N}):K(\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}}^{N})\to K(\Sigma_{i_{1},...,i_{d}}^{N})[1]
is given by

(4.30)

\hskip-28.45274ptK(d_{\delta}^{N}):=\sum K(\rho_{k}^{\Sigma\oplus\Sigma_{\infty}}(\cdot,b_{i,i_{2}},...,b_{i_{k-1},j})^{N})\otimes(B_{i,i_{2}}...B_{i_{k-1},j})\quad\in\quad\bigoplus_{i,j\in I_{M}}\Hom(K(I_{i}),K(I_{j})[1])\otimes\Hom(V_{i},V_{j})\ ,

where the sum is over the same index set as in Equation
4.28
above.

We now give a concrete description of the equivalence of this data with that of a representation of the extended quiver
Q_{M}
, which is by definition given by a (finite rank, in the sense of Definition
4.15
) module over the path algebra
\Lambda_{M}=(\otimes^{\bullet}_{S_{M}}\bar{\Sigma}_{M}[1])^{\vee}
, as ensured by the equivalence of Theorem
4.20
between
\textup{PervCoh}_{M}^{\textup{p}}(Y)^{T}
and
\Lambda_{M}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{fr}}
.

The K theory class of an object
H\in\textup{PervCoh}_{M}^{\textup{p}}(Y)^{T}
is determined by the multiplicites
d_{i}\in\mathbb{N}
for
i\in I
of the simple factors
F_{i}
together with the multiplicity
d_{\infty}\in\mathbb{N}
of the auxiliary object
M
. These multiplicities correspond to those of the finite dimensional simple
\Lambda_{M}
modules
S_{i}
for
i\in I
together with that of the remaining finite rank generator
S_{\infty}
. The extended quiver representation corresponding to
H
is then determined by a
{\textbf{d}}=(d_{i})_{i\in I_{M}}
dimensional
S_{M}
module

V=\bigoplus_{i\in V_{Q_{M}}}V_{i}=V_{\infty}\oplus\bigoplus_{i\in V_{Q}}V_{i}

together with a map

(4.31)

{\mathbb{K}}\langle E_{Q_{M}}\rangle^{0}=(\Sigma_{M}^{1})^{\vee}\to{\underline{\textup{End}}}_{S_{M}{\textup{-BiMod}}}(V)

of
S_{M}
bimodules, such that the induced map from the cohomological degree zero component of the quasi-free resolution of the path algebra
\Lambda_{M}^{0}=\otimes_{S_{M}}^{\bullet}{\mathbb{K}}\langle E_{Q_{M}}\rangle^{0}
to
{\underline{\textup{End}}}_{S{\textup{-BiMod}}}(V)
maps the ideal of relations in the quiver
Q_{M}
to zero.

The map of Equation
4.31
can equivalently be interpreted as an element

\delta=\sum_{i,j\in I_{M}}b_{ij}\otimes B_{ij}\quad\in\quad\Sigma_{M}^{1}\otimes{\underline{\textup{End}}}(V)=\bigoplus_{i,j\in I_{M}}\ {}_{i}(\Sigma_{M})_{j}\otimes\Hom(V_{i},V_{j})\ ,

which determines a cohomological degree
+1
endomorphism
d_{B}:\tilde{H}\to\tilde{H}[1]
of the perverse coherent complex

(4.32)

\tilde{H}:=\bigoplus_{i\in I_{M}}K(I_{i})\otimes_{S_{i}}V_{i}\ \in\textup{PervCoh}_{M}^{\textup{p}}(Y)^{\mathbb{C}^{\times}}\quad\quad\text{, or}\quad\quad\tilde{H}:=\bigoplus_{i\in I_{M}}\hat{K}(I_{i})\otimes_{S_{i}}V_{i}\ \in\textup{PervCoh}_{M}^{\textup{p}}(\hat{Y})

in the ungraded case, by the formula

(4.33)

d_{B}=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z},\ i,i_{2},...,i_{k-1},j\in I_{M}}K(\rho_{k}^{\Sigma\oplus\Sigma_{\infty}}(\cdot,b_{i,i_{2}},...,b_{i_{k-1},j})^{N})\otimes(B_{i,i_{2}}...B_{i_{k-1},j})\ .

We can now state the desired generalization of Propositions
3.26
and
3.29
:

Proposition 4.26
.

Let
\tilde{H}\in\textup{PervCoh}_{M}^{\textup{p}}(Y)^{T}
be as in Equation
4.32
and fix

B:=(B_{ij})_{i,j\in I_{M}}\quad\quad\text{with}\quad\quad B_{ij}=(B_{ij}^{\alpha}\in\Hom(V_{i},V_{j}))_{\alpha\in\mathcal{B}_{ij}}\ .

The following are equivalent:

•

the induced map
d_{B}:\tilde{H}\to\tilde{H}[1]
of Equation
4.33
satisfies
d_{B}^{2}=0
, and

•

the induced map
\rho:(\Sigma^{1}_{M})^{\vee}\to{\underline{\textup{End}}}(V)
of Equation
4.31
defines a representation of the graded DG quiver
Q_{M}
.

Further, when these conditions hold, the resulting complex
(\tilde{H},d_{B})
is a projective resolution of the object
H\in\textup{PervCoh}_{M}^{\textup{p}}(Y)^{T}
corresponding to the extended quiver representation
V\in\Lambda_{M}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{fr}}
.

Similarly, for
\tilde{H}\in\textup{PervCoh}_{M}^{\textup{p}}(\hat{Y})
as in Equation
4.32
, the following are equivalent:

•

the induced map
d_{B}:\tilde{H}\to\tilde{H}[1]
of Equation
4.33
satisfies
d_{B}^{2}=0
, and

•

the induced map
\rho:(\Sigma^{1}_{M})^{\vee}\to{\underline{\textup{End}}}_{S{\textup{-BiMod}}}(V)
of Equation
4.31
defines a nilpotent representation of the DG quiver
Q_{M}
.

Further, when these conditions hold, the resulting complex
(\tilde{H},d_{B})
is a projective resolution of the object
H\in\textup{PervCoh}_{M}(\hat{Y})
corresponding to the extended quiver representation
V\in\Lambda_{M}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{Fr}}
.

Proof.

The proof is the same as that of Proposition
3.29
,
mutatis mutandis
.
∎

4.5.
Moduli spaces of perverse coherent extensions and extended quivers

Let
Q_{{M}}
be an extended quiver, with vertex set
V_{Q_{{M}}}=V_{Q}\cup\{\infty\}
and edge set
E_{Q_{{M}}}=E_{Q}\cup E_{\infty}
, where
E_{\infty}
denotes all edges of the extended quiver with
\infty
as at least one of its source and target vertices. The free path algebra of the extended quiver is given by

\mathbb{K}Q_{{M}}=\otimes^{\bullet}_{S_{{M}}}\mathbb{K}\langle E_{Q_{{M}}}\rangle\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad S_{{M}}=\oplus_{i\in V_{Q}}S_{i}\oplus S_{\infty}=\oplus_{I\in I}\mathbb{K}\oplus S_{\infty}\ .

For each dimension vector
{\textbf{d}}=({\textbf{d}}_{0},d_{\infty})\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{M}}}=\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}\times\mathbb{N}
for the extended quiver, define

X_{{\textbf{d}}}(Q_{{M}})=\bigoplus_{i,j\in I_{{M}}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma^{1}_{j}\otimes\Hom(\mathbb{K}^{d_{i}},\mathbb{K}^{d_{j}})\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad G_{{\textbf{d}}}(Q_{{M}})=\prod_{i\in V_{Q_{{M}}}}{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{i}}(S_{i})\ .

The stack of representations
\mathfrak{M}(Q_{M})
of the free
S_{M}
-algebra on the extended quiver
Q_{{M}}
is defined as the disjoint union of the quotient stacks

\mathfrak{M}(Q_{{M}})=\bigsqcup_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{{M}}}}}\mathfrak{M}_{{\textbf{d}}}(Q_{{M}})\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}_{{\textbf{d}}}(Q_{{M}})=\left[X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{{M}})/G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{{M}})\right]\ .

Remark 4.27
.

Note that for
{\textbf{d}}=({\textbf{d}}_{0},0)\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{M}}}=\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}\times\mathbb{N}
, we have tautological identifications

\bigoplus_{i,j\in I}\ {}_{i}\Sigma^{1}_{j}\otimes\Hom(\mathbb{K}^{d_{i}},\mathbb{K}^{d_{j}})=\bigoplus_{e\in E_{Q}}\Hom({\mathbb{K}}^{d_{s(e)}},{\mathbb{K}}^{d_{t(e)}})\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{i}}(S_{i})={\textup{Gl}}_{d_{i}}(\mathbb{K})\

for
i\in V_{Q}
, so that in this case the definitions of
X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}),\ G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})
and
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})
reduce to the standard definitions of
X_{\textbf{d}}(Q),\ G_{\textbf{d}}(Q)
and
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}(Q)
given in Section
2.4
.

Let
{\underline{\textup{End}}}(S_{M}^{\textbf{d}}):=\Hom(S_{M}^{\textbf{d}},S_{M}^{\textbf{d}})\in S_{M}{\textup{-BiMod}}
denote the matrix algebra on

S_{M}^{\textbf{d}}:=\bigoplus_{i\in V_{Q_{M}}}S_{i}^{d_{i}}=\mathbb{K}^{{\textbf{d}}_{0}}\oplus S_{\infty}^{d_{\infty}}

with its natural
S_{M}
bimodule structure, and note that there are canonical identifications

X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})\cong\Hom_{S_{M}{\textup{-BiMod}}}({\mathbb{K}}\langle E_{Q_{M}}\rangle,{\underline{\textup{End}}}(S_{M}^{\textbf{d}}))\cong\Hom_{\textup{Alg}_{\textup{Ass}}(S_{M}{\textup{-BiMod}})}({\mathbb{K}}{Q_{M}},{\underline{\textup{End}}}(S_{M}^{\textbf{d}}))\ ,

so that we have

\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})({\mathbb{K}})\cong\{V\in S_{M}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{Fr}},\ \varphi\in\Hom_{\textup{Alg}_{\textup{Ass}}(S{\textup{-BiMod}})}({\mathbb{K}}Q_{M},{\underline{\textup{End}}}(V))\ |\ \dim V={\textbf{d}}\ \}\ ,

that is, the groupoid of geometric points of
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}
is the maximal subgroupoid of the category of modules over the free path algebra
\mathbb{K}Q_{M}
with underlying
S_{M}
module a direct sum of free
S_{i}
modules of finite rank
d
.

Let
R_{M}\subset\mathbb{K}Q_{M}
be the ideal generated by the image of the Koszul differential

d_{\Lambda_{M}}^{-1}:\Lambda_{M}^{-1}\to\Lambda_{M}^{0}=\mathbb{K}Q_{M}\ ,

and for each
{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{M}}}
define the closed subvariety
Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{{M}},R_{{M}})\subset X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})
by

\displaystyle Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{{M}},I_{{M}})

\displaystyle=\{\varphi\in\Hom_{\textup{Alg}_{\textup{Ass}}(S_{M}{\textup{-BiMod}})}({\mathbb{K}}{Q_{M}},{\underline{\textup{End}}}(S_{M}^{\textbf{d}}))\ |\ \varphi(I_{M})=\{0\}\ \subset{\underline{\textup{End}}}(S_{M}^{\textbf{d}})\}

\displaystyle=\Hom_{\textup{Alg}_{\textup{Ass}}(S_{M}{\textup{-BiMod}})}(\Lambda_{M},{\underline{\textup{End}}}(S_{M}^{\textbf{d}}))

.

Note that
Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},I_{M})
is
G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})
invariant, as the condition that the corresponding map to
{\underline{\textup{End}}}(V)
satisfies
\varphi(I_{M})=\{0\}
is well defined, independent of the choice of isomorphism
V\cong S_{M}^{\textbf{d}}
. The stack of representations
\mathfrak{M}(Q_{M},R_{M})
of the extended quiver
(Q_{M},R_{M})
is defined analogously as the disjoint union of the quotient stacks

\mathfrak{M}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\bigsqcup_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\left[Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})/G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})\right]

and we have the analogous description of the geometric points

\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})({\mathbb{K}})=\{V\in S_{M}{\textup{-BiMod}},\ \varphi\in\Hom_{\textup{Alg}_{\textup{Ass}}(S_{M}{\textup{-BiMod}})}({\mathbb{K}}Q_{M}/R_{M},{\underline{\textup{End}}}(V))\ |\ \dim_{S_{M}}V={\textbf{d}}\ \}

as parameterizing the modules over the path algebra
{\mathbb{K}}Q_{M}/R_{M}=\Lambda_{M}
with underlying
S_{M}
module a direct sum of free
S_{i}
modules of finite rank
d
.

There are subspaces
X_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M})\subset X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})
defined by

X_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M})=\{\varphi\in\Hom_{\textup{Alg}_{\textup{Ass}}(S_{M}{\textup{-BiMod}})}({\mathbb{K}}Q_{M},{\underline{\textup{End}}}(S_{M}^{\textbf{d}}))\ |\ \varphi(({\mathbb{K}}Q_{M})_{(n)})=\{0\}\ \subset{\underline{\textup{End}}}(S_{M}^{\textbf{d}})\ \textup{for $n\gg 0$}\}\ ,

and in turn a substack
\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M})\subset\mathfrak{M}(Q_{M})
defined by

\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M})=\bigsqcup_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{M}}}}\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M})=\left[X_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M})/G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})\right]\ .

Similarly, there are closed subvarieties
Z_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\subset X_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M})
defined by

Z_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\times_{X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})}X_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M})

and in turn a closed substack
\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\subset\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M})
defined by

\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\bigsqcup_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{M}}}}\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\left[Z_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M},R_{M})/G_{\textbf{d}}(Q)\right]\ .

We now state the main result of this section, which is the full statement of Theorem A from the introduction. As in Section
3.6
, we introduce the notation

\mathfrak{M}(Y,M):=\mathfrak{M}_{\textup{PervCoh}_{M}^{\textup{p}}(\hat{Y})}\ ,

and we have:

Theorem 4.28
.

Let
M\in\textup{PervCoh}^{\textup{p}}(Y)^{T}
be an object satisfying the hypotheses in Section
4.1
, and let
Q_{M}
be the associated extended quiver. There is an equivalence of algebraic stacks

(4.34)

\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M},R_{{M}})\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathfrak{M}(Y,M)

where the induced equivalence of groupoids of
\mathbb{K}
points is defined on objects by

\hskip-28.45274pt(V_{i},B_{ij})\mapsto\left(\tilde{H}:=\bigoplus_{i\in I_{M}}K(I_{i})\otimes_{S_{i}}V_{i}\ ,\ d_{B}:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z},\ i,i_{2},...,i_{k-1},j\in I_{M}}K(\rho_{k}^{\Sigma\oplus\Sigma_{\infty}}(\cdot,b_{i,i_{2}},...,b_{i_{k-1},j})^{N})\otimes(B_{i,i_{2}}...B_{i_{k-1},j})\right)\ ,

in the notation of Section
4.4
.

Similarly, this induces an equivalence of the
T
fixed points

(4.35)

\mathfrak{M}(Q_{M},R_{M})^{T}\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathfrak{M}_{\textup{PervCoh}_{M}^{\textup{p}}(Y)^{T}}\ .

The main remaining ingredient of the proof is the following lemma:

Lemma 4.29
.

Let
\Lambda_{M}=\mathbb{K}\langle Q_{M}\rangle/R_{M}
be the path algebra of the extended quiver
Q_{M}
and
\hat{\Lambda}_{M}
be its completion. There is an equivalence of algebraic stacks

\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{{M}},R_{{M}})\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathfrak{M}_{\hat{\Lambda}_{{M}}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{Fr}}}\ .

Proof.

Let
R
be a commutative ring with
T={\textup{Spec}\ }R
, recall that
W={\textup{Spf}\ }S_{\infty}\subset\hat{X}
denotes the formal subscheme of
\hat{X}
on which
\pi_{*}M
is supported, and fix
{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{M}}}
. The groupoid of
R
points of the component
\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{{M}},I_{{M}})
of the left hand side is given by

\displaystyle\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{{M}},I_{{M}})(R)

\displaystyle=[Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},I_{M})/G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})](R)

\displaystyle=\{P\in\Bun_{G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})}(T)\ ,\ \varphi\in\Gamma(T,P\times_{G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})}X_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M}))\ |\ \varphi(I_{M}\otimes R)=\{0\}\ \}\ .\

Note that the underlying
G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})={\textup{Gl}}_{{\textbf{d}}_{0}}(\mathbb{K})\times{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(S_{\infty})
bundle
P
over
R
is equivalent to a rank
d_{i}
vector bundle
V_{i}
over
T
for each
i\in V_{Q}
together with a rank
d_{\infty}
vector bundle
V_{\infty}
over
T\times W
, trivializable over
\{t\}\times W
for each
\mathbb{K}
point
t\in T(\mathbb{K})
. Under this identification, the section
\varphi
is equivalent to a collection of sections of the associated endomorphism bundle

(4.36)

\varphi\in\bigoplus_{i,j\in I_{M}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma_{j}^{1}\otimes_{S_{i}\otimes S_{j}^{\textup{op}}}\Gamma(T,{\underline{\textup{Hom}}}(V_{i},V_{j})\ )

satisfying the relations generating the ideal
I_{M}
, such that for each
\mathbb{K}
point
t\in T(\mathbb{K})
, the induced morphism of associative algebras
\Lambda_{M}\to{\underline{\textup{End}}}(V_{t})
has nilpotent image, where
V_{t}
denotes the fibre of
V=\oplus_{i\in I_{M}}V_{i}
at
t
.

Alternatively, the groupoid of
R
points of
\mathfrak{M}_{\hat{\Lambda}_{{M}}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{Fr}}}
is by definition given by

\mathfrak{M}_{\hat{\Lambda}_{{M}}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{Fr}}}(R)=\{V\in\textup{Ind}(\hat{\Lambda}_{M}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{Fr}})_{R}\ |\ \textup{$V$ is flat over $R$ and compact }\}\ ,

where we recall that
\mathcal{C}_{R}
denotes the category of
R
module objects internal to
\mathcal{C}
, as in Definition
3.30
.

The compact objects of
\textup{Ind}(\hat{\Lambda}_{M}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{Fr}})_{R}
are
\hat{\Lambda}_{M}\otimes_{\mathbb{K}}R
modules with underlying
S_{M}
module given as a colimit of free modules of finite rank over
S_{M}
, which are finitely generated as
\hat{\Lambda}_{M}\otimes_{\mathbb{K}}R
modules. These conditions together imply that the underlying
S_{M}\otimes_{\mathbb{K}}R
module is finitely generated.

Given an object
V\in\textup{Ind}(\hat{\Lambda}_{M}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{Fr}})_{R}
, let
V=\oplus_{i\in V_{Q}}V_{i}\oplus V_{\infty}
denote the natural decomposition as a module over
S_{M}=S\oplus S_{\infty}
.
If
V
is compact, then each
V_{i}
defines a finitely generated
R
module, and
V_{\infty}
a finitely generated
S_{\infty}\otimes_{\mathbb{K}}R
module such that
(V_{\infty})_{t}=V_{\infty}\otimes_{R}\mathbb{K}
is projective for each
\mathbb{K}
point
t\in T(\mathbb{K})
; the latter follows from the fact that the category of compact objects of the ind completion of a category
\mathcal{C}
is given by the Karoubi completion of
\mathcal{C}
, and the Karoubi completion of the category of free
S_{\infty}
modules is the category of projective
S_{\infty}
modules. Moreover, since
S_{\infty}
is a local ring, projective and finitely generated implies free, so that
(V_{\infty})_{t}
is free of finite rank over
S_{\infty}
for each
\mathbb{K}
point
t\in T(\mathbb{K})
.

Finally, for
V\in\textup{Ind}(\hat{\Lambda}_{M}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{Fr}})_{R}^{\textup{c}}
compact, the condition that
V
be flat over
R
corresponds under the above identifications to the condition that each
V_{i}
is flat as an
R
module for
i\in V_{Q_{M}}
. Thus, for each
i\in V_{Q}
,
V_{i}
defines a finitely generated, projective
R
module or equivalently a vector bundle on
T
of finite rank
d_{i}
. Similarly,
V_{\infty}
defines a vector bundle on
T\times W
of finite rank
d_{\infty}
such that
(V_{\infty})_{t}
is trivializable for each
t\in T(\mathbb{K})
.

Thus, we have identified the
S_{M}\otimes_{\mathbb{K}}R
module underlying an object
V\in\mathfrak{M}_{\hat{\Lambda}_{{M}}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{Fr}}}(R)
with the collection of vector bundles underlying an object in the groupoid of
R
points
\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{{M}},I_{{M}})(R)
. The additional data required to define the
\hat{\Lambda}_{M}\otimes R
module structure on
V
is evidently equivalent to that of
\varphi
in Equation
4.36
; this completes the proof of the lemma.
∎

We now conclude the proof of Theorem
4.28
using the lemma and explain some implications of the result:

Proof.

(of Theorem
4.28
)
The definition of the moduli of objects functor is evidently natural with respect to equivalences of categories, so that we obtain a canonical equivalence of algebraic stacks

\mathfrak{M}_{\hat{\Lambda}_{{M}}{\textup{-Mod}}_{\textup{Fr}}}\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathfrak{M}_{\textup{PervCoh}_{M}^{\textup{p}}(\hat{Y})},

by the equivalence of Theorem
4.20
. Composing with the equivalence of algebraic stacks of Lemma
4.29
yields the desired equivalence of Equation
4.34
, and the induced equivalence on groupoids of
\mathbb{K}
points is defined on objects by the claimed formula, by Proposition
4.26
.
∎

For
Q_{M}
the extended quiver corresponding to the object

, let

, and similarly define

X_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})=\ _{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}\otimes{\textup{End}}(\mathbb{K}^{d_{\infty}})\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})=[X_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})/{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(S_{\infty})]\ ,

as well as closed subvarieties
Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})\subset X_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})
and corresponding closed substacks
\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})\subset\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})
by

\hskip-28.45274ptZ_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})=X_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})\times_{X_{{\textbf{d}}}(Q_{M})}Z_{{\textbf{d}}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})=[Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})/{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(S_{\infty})]\ ,

where
{\textbf{d}}=(\textbf{0},d_{\infty})\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{M}}}=\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}\times\mathbb{N}
.

Remark 4.31
.

Note that for
{\textbf{d}}=(\textbf{0},d_{\infty})\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{M}}}=\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}\times\mathbb{N}
, we have tautological identifications

X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})=X_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})={\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(S_{\infty})

so that in this case the definitions of
X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})
and
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})
reduce to the definitions of
X_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})
and
\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})
given in the preceding paragraph.

.

Example 4.33
.

Let
W\subset\hat{Y}
denote a smooth, toric subvariety and
M=\mathcal{O}_{W}
, so that
S_{\infty}=H^{0}(W,\mathcal{O}_{W})
. Then using the Koszul resolution, we can compute

{}_{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}\cong\Ext^{1}(\mathcal{O}_{W},\mathcal{O}_{W})\cong H^{0}(W,N_{W/Y})\ ,

the space of global sections of the normal bundle
N_{W/Y}
to
W
in
Y
. Moreover, the space

Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})\subset X_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})\cong H^{0}(W,N_{W/Y})\otimes{\textup{End}}(\mathbb{K}^{d_{\infty}})

identifies with the space of global
N_{W/Y}
-twisted Higgs fields on the trivial bundle
\mathcal{O}_{W}^{\oplus d_{\infty}}
. Thus, the stack of nilpotent representations of the quiver with relations
(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})
is given by

\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})=\left[Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})/{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(S_{\infty})\right]\cong\textup{Higgs}^{\textup{nil}}_{d_{\infty}}(W,N_{W/Y})_{0}\ ,

the stack of nilpotent
N_{W/Y}
-twisted Higgs bundles on
W
of rank
d_{\infty}
with underlying vector bundle isomorphic to the trivial bundle, though without such an isomorphism fixed.

Thus, in this example, we find that Corollary
4.32
reduces to the relevant variant of the spectral correspondence, giving an equivalence between the above-described stack of Higgs bundles and the stack of coherent sheaves on
\hat{Y}
isomorphic to an iterated extension of the structure sheaf
\mathcal{O}_{W}
.

4.6.
Framing structures

For an arbitrary element

\delta=\sum_{i,j\in R_{M}}b_{ij}\otimes B_{ij}\quad\in\quad\Sigma_{M}^{1}\otimes{\underline{\textup{End}}}(V)=\bigoplus_{i,j\in R_{M}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma_{j}\otimes\Hom(V_{i},V_{j})\ ,

consider the decomposition
V=V_{\textbf{0}}\oplus V_{\infty}:=\left(\oplus_{i\in I}V_{i}\right)\oplus V_{\infty}
and the induced decomposition

\delta=\ _{0}\delta_{0}+\ _{\infty}\delta_{0}+\ _{0}\delta_{\infty}+\ _{\infty}\delta_{\infty}\quad\in\quad\Sigma^{1}\otimes{\underline{\textup{End}}}(V)=\bigoplus_{i,j\in\{\textbf{0},\infty\}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma_{j}\otimes\Hom(V_{i},V_{j})\ .

We now formulate an additional hypothesis on the object
M\in{\textup{D}}^{b}\textup{Coh}(Y)^{T}
, which will be necessary for the results of this section: we require that the
i=j=\infty
component of the Maurer-Cartan equations on
\delta
determined by
\Sigma_{M}
, in the sense of Equation
2.9
, satisfies

(4.37)

\ _{\infty}\left(\sum_{t\in\mathbb{N}}m_{t}^{\mathfrak{gl}_{{\textbf{d}}}(\Sigma_{M})}(\delta^{\otimes t})\right)\ \!\!\!_{\infty}\ =\sum_{t\in\mathbb{N}}m_{t}^{\mathfrak{gl}_{d_{\infty}}(\!\!\ _{\infty}\Sigma_{\infty})}((_{\infty}\delta_{\infty})^{\otimes t})\ \in\mathfrak{gl}_{d_{\infty}}(\!\!\ _{\infty}\Sigma_{\infty})\ ,

that is, the
(\infty,\infty)
component of the Maurer-Cartan operator for
\Sigma_{M}
evaluated on
\delta
is equal to the Maurer-Cartan operator for
\Sigma_{\infty}
evaluated on the
(\infty,\infty)
component of
\delta
.

Proposition 4.34
.

Let
M\in{\textup{D}}^{b}\textup{Coh}(Y)^{T}
satisfy the condition of Equation
4.37
, in addition to the usual hypotheses introduced in Section
4.1
. Then there exists a canonical map of stacks

\mathfrak{M}(Q_{M},R_{M})\to\mathfrak{M}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})\quad\quad\text{defined by}\quad\quad(V_{i}\ ,B_{ij})_{i,j\in R_{M}}\mapsto(V_{\infty}\ ,B_{\infty\infty})\ .

Proof.

The projection map to the direct summand corresponding to
i=j=\infty
defines a canonical map

X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})=\bigoplus_{i,j\in I_{{M}}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma^{1}_{j}\otimes\Hom(\mathbb{K}^{d_{i}},\mathbb{K}^{d_{j}})\to\ _{\infty}\Sigma_{\infty}^{1}\otimes{\textup{End}}(\mathbb{K}^{d_{\infty}})=X_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})

which evidently induces a map on quotient stacks

\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})\to\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})\ .

It remains to check that the restriction of the projection map to
Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\subset X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})
defines a map

Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\to Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})\quad\quad\text{and thus a map}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\to\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})\ ,

as desired, on the corresponding closed substacks of the above quotient stacks. The left hand side of Equation
4.37
is one of the generators of the defining ideal of the subvariety
Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\subset X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})
, and thus the equality with the right hand side, which generates the ideal defining
Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})\subset X_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})
, implies the result.
∎

Under the hypotheses of the preceding proposition, we also have:

Corollary 4.35
.

There exists a canonical map of stacks

\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\to\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{nil}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})\quad\quad\text{defined by}\quad\quad(V_{i}\ ,B_{ij})_{i,j\in I_{M}}\mapsto(V_{\infty}\ ,B_{\infty\infty})\ .

Proof.

The projection map
X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})\to X_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})
evidently maps
X^{\textup{nil}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})
to
X^{\textup{nil}}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})
, and the result follows readily from the proof of Proposition
4.34
.
∎

We have the following equivalent geometric form of the corollary:

Corollary 4.36
.

There exists a canonical map of stacks

\mathfrak{M}(Y,M)\to\mathfrak{M}_{\textup{Filt}(M)}

defined by forgetting the compactly supported composition factors and remembering only the underlying iterated extension of
M
.

Proof.

This is equivalent to the statement of the preceding corollary, under the identifications of Theorem
4.28
and Corollary
4.32
. Note that while the operation on complexes of coherent sheaves defining the map is evidently not well-defined in general, the geometric content of Proposition
4.34
above is that this operation is well defined under the given hypotheses.
∎

Definition 4.37
.

A
framing structure
for
M
of rank
d_{\infty}
is a
\mathbb{K}
-point

{\textup{f}}\in Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})(\mathbb{K})\ .

Given a framing structure
f
for
M
of rank
d_{\infty}

\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}
over
\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})
by

\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}=\left[\{{\textup{f}}\}/G_{\textup{f}}\right]\cong\left[\mathbb{O}_{\textup{f}}/{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(S_{\infty})\right]\ \to\ \mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})\ ,

where
G_{\textup{f}}=\textup{Stab}_{{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(S_{\infty})}({\textup{f}})
denotes the subgroup of
{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(S_{\infty})
stabilizing the point
f
, and
\mathbb{O}_{\textup{f}}\subset Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})
denotes the orbit of
f
under
{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(S_{\infty})
. Similarly, we define the stack
\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}
over
\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})
by

\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}=\left[\{{\textup{f}}\}/G^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}\right]\cong\left[\mathbb{O}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}/{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(\mathbb{K})\right]\ \to\ \mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})\ ,

where
G^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}=\textup{Stab}_{{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(\mathbb{K})}({\textup{f}})
denotes the subgroup of
{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(\mathbb{K})
stabilizing the point
f
, and
\mathbb{O}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}\subset Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})
denotes the orbit of
f
under
{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(\mathbb{K})
.

Moreover, for any
{\textbf{d}}=(d_{i})\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}

-framed representations of

of dimension

\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\mathfrak{M}_{({\textbf{d}},d_{\infty})}(Q_{M},R_{M})\times_{\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})}\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}

-framed representations of

by

\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\bigsqcup_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\ ,

as usual. Similarly, we define the stack of
\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}^{\textup{c}}
-framed representations of
Q_{M}
by

\hskip-28.45274pt\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\bigsqcup_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\mathfrak{M}_{({\textbf{d}},d_{\infty})}(Q_{M},R_{M})\times_{\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})}\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}\ .

More explicitly, we introduce the space

\displaystyle X^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})

\displaystyle=X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})\times_{X_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty})}\{{\textup{f}}\}

\displaystyle\cong\bigoplus_{i,j\in V_{Q}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma^{1}_{j}\otimes\Hom(\mathbb{K}^{d_{i}},\mathbb{K}^{d_{j}})\oplus\bigoplus_{i\in V_{Q}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}\otimes\Hom(\mathbb{K}^{d_{i}},\mathbb{K}^{d_{\infty}})\oplus\bigoplus_{j\in V_{Q}}\ {}_{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{j}\otimes\Hom(\mathbb{K}^{d_{\infty}},\mathbb{K}^{d_{j}})

as well as the closed subvariety

, defined by

Z^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\times_{Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})}\{{\textup{f}}\}\ .

Then the moduli stacks of
\mathcal{F}_{{\textup{f}}}
-framed and
\mathcal{F}_{f}^{\textup{c}}
-framed representations of
Q_{M}
of dimension

are given by

\hskip-28.45274pt\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\left[Z^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})/(G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{Y})\times G_{\textup{f}})\right]\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\left[Z^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})/(G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{Y})\times G_{\textup{f}}^{\textup{c}})\right]\ ,

respectively.

Finally, we define the stack of

by

\mathfrak{M}^{{\textup{f}}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\bigsqcup_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}\mathfrak{M}^{{\textup{f}}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}^{{\textup{f}}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\mathfrak{M}_{({\textbf{d}},d_{\infty})}(Q_{M},R_{M})\times_{\mathfrak{M}_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})}\{{\textup{f}}\}

and the analogous concrete description is simply given by

\mathfrak{M}^{{\textup{f}}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\left[Z^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})/G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{Y})\right]\ .

We can also define the corresponding equivalent geometric moduli stacks

(4.38)

\displaystyle\mathfrak{M}^{{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)

\displaystyle=\bigsqcup_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)

\displaystyle\textup{where}\quad\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)

\displaystyle=\mathfrak{M}_{({\textbf{d}},d_{\infty})}(Y,M)\times_{\mathfrak{M}_{\textup{Filt}(M),d_{\infty}}}\{{\textup{f}}\}

,

(4.39)

\displaystyle\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)

\displaystyle\textup{where}\quad\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)

\displaystyle=\mathfrak{M}_{({\textbf{d}},d_{\infty})}(Y,M)\times_{\mathfrak{M}_{\textup{Filt}(M),d_{\infty}}}\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}

,

(4.40)

\displaystyle\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)

\displaystyle=\bigsqcup_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)

\displaystyle\textup{where}\quad\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)

.

We can now give the framed analogue of Theorem
4.28
, which establishes a special case of Conjecture 10.3.5 a) in
[
KS11b
]
:

Theorem 4.38
.

Let
M\in\textup{PervCoh}^{\textup{p}}(Y)^{T}
as in Theorem
4.28
and let
f
be a framing structure for
M
. There is a canonical framed quiver with potential
(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
and an equivalence of algebraic stacks

(4.41)

\mathfrak{M}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathfrak{M}^{{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)\ ,

where the induced equivalence of groupoids of
\mathbb{K}
points is defined on objects by

\hskip-28.45274pt(V_{i},B_{ij})\mapsto\left(\tilde{H}:=\bigoplus_{i\in I_{M}}K(I_{i})\otimes_{S_{i}}V_{i}\ ,\ d_{B}:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z},\ i,i_{2},...,i_{k-1},j\in I_{M}}K(\rho_{k}^{\Sigma\oplus\Sigma_{\infty}}(\cdot,b_{i,i_{2}},...,b_{i_{k-1},j})^{N})\otimes(B_{i,i_{2}}...B_{i_{k-1},j})\right)\ ,

in the notation of Section
4.4
.

Proof.

By Theorem
4.28
and Corollary
4.32
, the desired result is equivalent to an equivalence of algebraic
\mathbb{K}
-stacks

\mathfrak{M}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathfrak{M}^{{\textup{f}}}(Q_{M},R_{M})

which we now construct.

The underlying quiver
Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}
is essentially the same as the extended quiver
Q_{M}
, but with the extended node corresponding to the object
M
considered as a framing node, and the edges from the extended node to itself excluded from the edge set; more formally, we define the set of internal vertices by
V_{Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}}=V_{Q_{Y}}
, and define the
\mathbb{K}
-linear span of the edge set to be

\mathbb{K}\langle E_{Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}}\rangle:=\bigoplus_{i,j\in V_{Q}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma_{j}^{\vee}[-1]\oplus\bigoplus_{i\in V_{Q}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma_{\infty}^{\vee}[-1]\oplus\bigoplus_{j\in V_{Q}}\ {}_{\infty}\Sigma_{j}^{\vee}[-1]\ .

Note that we evidently have an identification of vector spaces

X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}):=\Hom_{S{\textup{-BiMod}}}(\mathbb{K}\langle E_{Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}}\rangle,{\underline{\textup{End}}}(\mathbb{K}^{\textbf{d}}))\cong X^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})\ .

Thus, it remains to check that the closed subvariety
Z^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})\subset X^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})
is given by the critical locus of a potential. In fact, the potential is given by a slight variant of the formula given in Example
2.35
, as follows: we fix a decomposition

{\textup{f}}=\sum_{\alpha}f_{\alpha}\otimes F_{\alpha}\ \in\ _{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}\otimes{\textup{End}}(\mathbb{K}^{d_{\infty}})

in terms of which the potential (which is evidently independent of this choice of decomposition) is given by

W_{M}^{\textup{f}}=\sum_{n\geq 1}\sum_{a_{1},...,a_{n+1}\in E_{Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}}\cup\{f_{\alpha}\}}\langle m_{n}^{\Sigma_{M}}(a_{1}^{\vee},...,a_{n}^{\vee}),a_{n+1}^{\vee}\rangle a_{1}\cdot...\cdot a_{n+1}\ ,

where we note that
E_{Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}}\cup\{f_{\alpha}\}\subset E_{Q_{M}}
, so that their duals define elements on which the
A_{\infty}
multiplication
m_{n}^{\Sigma_{M}}:\Sigma_{M}^{\otimes n}\to\Sigma_{M}[2-n]
can be evaluated. We then interpret the variables
a_{i}
corresponding to edges
a_{i}\in E_{Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}}\subset E_{Q_{M}}
as the usual defining variables in the potential, while the variables
a_{i}=f_{\alpha}\in\ _{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}
are defined to evaluate to the fixed linear maps
F_{\alpha}
when defining the induced potential
W^{\textup{f}}_{M,{\textbf{d}}}:X^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})\to\mathbb{K}
for any
{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}
. In analogy with Example
2.35
, the critical locus equations induce the Maurer-Cartan equations for
\Sigma_{M}
, with the modification of the variables corresponding to
\{{\textup{f}}_{\alpha}\}
inducing the specialization at
{\textup{f}}\in Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},I_{\infty})
, so that we have that

Z^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M},R_{M})=\textup{crit}(W^{\textup{f}}_{M,{\textbf{d}}})\subset X^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M})\ ,

as desired.
∎

Finally, we give a brief explanation of the geometric interpretation of these stacks. By Corollary
4.36
, we have the following modular descriptions of the spaces of
\mathbb{K}
points:

•

For
\mathfrak{M}^{{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)
, a perverse coherent extension equipped with an isomorphism from the underlying iterated extension of
M
to that determined by
f
.

•

For
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)
, a perverse coherent extension equipped with an isomorphism from the underlying iterated extension of
M
to a complex of sheaves of the form
(K(I_{\infty})\otimes_{\mathbb{K}}W,\ d)
where
W
is a
\mathbb{K}
vector space of dimension
d_{\infty}
and
d
an auxiliary differential which is conjugate under
{\textup{Gl}}(W)
to the differential determined by
f
.

•

For
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)
, a perverse coherent extension such that the underlying iterated extension of
M
is isomorphic to that determined by
f
.

We now explain the distinction between these variants in the simplest examples, though we note that several more involved examples are given in Section
4.7
below. We fix the dimension vector to be
{\textbf{d}}=\bf 0\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}
, so that by Corollary
4.32
, we have

\mathfrak{M}_{(\textbf{0},d_{\infty})}(Y,M)\cong\mathfrak{M}_{\textup{Filt}(M),d_{\infty}}\ ,

that is, the (unframed) moduli of perverse coherent extensions is given by the moduli stack of objects in the full subcategory on objects admitting filtration with subquotients isomorphic to
M
of total multiplicity
d_{\infty}
. In turn, this implies that the framed moduli spaces are simply given by

\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{0}}^{{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)\cong\{{\textup{f}}\}\ ,\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{0}}^{\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)\cong\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}\ ,\text{ and}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{0}}^{\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)\cong\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}\ .

We now explain these isomorphisms explicitly in some special cases:

Example 4.39
.

Let the framing object be
M=\mathcal{O}_{\hat{Y}}
the structure sheaf of
\hat{Y}
. Since the structure sheaf does not admit any non-trivial extensions with itself, the only possible framing structure is given by
{\textup{f}}=0
, and
\mathfrak{M}_{(\bf{0},d_{\infty})}(Y,M)
is equivalent to the moduli stack of objects which are isomorphic to
\mathcal{O}_{\hat{Y}}^{\oplus d_{\infty}}
. Thus, in this case, we have that
\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}}_{(\bf{0},d_{\infty})}(Y,M)\cong\mathfrak{M}_{(\bf{0},d_{\infty})}(Y,M)
is given by the moduli stack of sheaves which are isomorphic to
\mathcal{O}_{\hat{Y}}^{\oplus d_{\infty}}
, which is evidently equivalent to
\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}=\left[\textup{pt}/{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(\mathcal{O}_{\hat{Y}})\right]
.

Similarly, we have that
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\mathcal{F}^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)
is the moduli stack of sheaves equipped with an isomorphism to
\mathcal{O}_{\hat{Y}}\otimes_{\mathbb{K}}W
for
W
a
\mathbb{K}
vector space of dimension
d_{\infty}
, which is evidently equivalent to

\mathcal{F}_{\textup{f}}^{\textup{c}}=\left[\textup{pt}/{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(\mathbb{K})\right]\ .

Finally, we have that
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}}}(Y,M)
is the moduli stack of sheaves equipped with an isomorphism to
\mathcal{O}_{\hat{Y}}^{\oplus d}
, which is evidently equivalent to just the single point
\{\mathcal{O}_{\hat{Y}}^{\oplus d_{\infty}}\}
corresponding to
{\textup{f}}=\{0\}
.

4.7.
Examples

In this section, we explain several examples of the construction of Theorem
4.38
and their relationships with previously known constructions of moduli spaces of coherent sheaves in terms of quivers.

Example 4.40
.

The most basic family of examples of perverse coherent extensions is the case when the extending object is given by
M=\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]
, the structure sheaf of the threefold shifted down in cohomological degree by one. As we explain in Section
6.1
below, in this case the definition of a perverse coherent extension is essentially equivalent to that of a perverse coherent system in the sense of Nagao-Nakajima
[
NN10
]
, and the resulting quivers generalize those studied in
loc. cit.
in the case of the resolved conifold following
[
Sze08
]
.

Indeed, for
M=\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]
, we have

{}_{\infty}\Sigma_{\infty}^{1}=0\quad\quad\ _{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{j}=0\quad\quad\ _{i}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}=\begin{cases}\mathbb{K}&\textup{if $i=0$}\\
\{0\}&\textup{otherwise}\end{cases}

independent of the threefold
Y
. Thus, the extended quivers are given by adding a single node and a single arrow from that node to the zeroth node of the quiver
Q_{Y}
. In the cases of Examples
3.34
,
3.35
, and
3.36
, the extended quivers
Q_{M}
are thus given by

.

to describe the moduli space of spiked instantons. Thus, the moduli stack of perverse coherent extensions provides a model for this moduli space defined purely in terms of algebraic geometry.

V_{\infty}^{1}=\{0\}
for simplicity, a framing structure
f

A_{\textup{f}}=(A_{2},A_{3},A_{2}^{3},A_{3}^{2})

.

3.35

Example 4.44
.

Let
Y=|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-2)|\to X={\textup{Spec}\ }{\mathbb{C}}[x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}]/(x_{1}x_{2}-x_{3}^{2})
, following Example
3.35
, and let
M=\mathcal{O}_{W}[1]
for
W=|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}|
. Then we have

{}_{0}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}=\mathbb{K}\quad\quad\ _{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{0}=\{0\}\quad\quad_{1}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}=\{0\}\quad\quad\ _{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{1}=\mathbb{K}^{2}\quad\quad\ _{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}=\{0\}

so that the extended quiver
Q_{M}

Example 4.45
.

Let
Y=|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-2)|\to X={\textup{Spec}\ }{\mathbb{C}}[x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}]/(x_{1}x_{2}-x_{3}^{2})
, following Example
3.35
, and let
M=\mathcal{O}_{W}[1]
for
W=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}|_{z=0}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-2)|_{z=0}\cong\mathbb{A}^{2}
. Then we have

{}_{0}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}=0\quad\quad\ _{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{0}=\mathbb{K}\quad\quad_{1}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}=\mathbb{K}\quad\quad\ _{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{1}=\{0\}\quad\quad\ _{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}=S_{\infty}

so that the extended quiver
Q_{M}
is given by

.

3.35

Example 4.48
.

Let
Y=X=\mathbb{C}^{3}
and let
M=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}}[1]
the shifted structure sheaf of the coordinate subspace
{\mathbb{C}}_{x}\subset\mathbb{C}^{3}
. Then we have

\ {}_{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{0}=\mathbb{K}^{2}\quad\quad\ _{0}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}=\mathbb{K}\quad\quad\ _{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}=S_{\infty}^{2}

so that the extended quiver
Q_{M}
is given by

Example 4.49
.

We can also consider the case where

M=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^{3}}[1]\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}_{x}}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{y}}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{z}}\ ,

using the
t
-structure of Example
4.13
. It is a straightforward generalization of the above computations to check that the resulting extended quiver is essentially that of
[
Jaf07
]
, which was apparently computed to describe the DT topological vertex. In particular, the framing vertex has four components

V_{\infty}=V_{\infty}^{0}\oplus V_{\infty}^{x}\oplus V_{\infty}^{y}\oplus V_{\infty}^{z}\,

corresponding to the four summands of
M
above.

In this example the moduli stack of framed perverse coherent extensions, rather than parameterizing maps from
\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}^{3}}
to an iterated extension of
\mathcal{O}_{\textup{pt}}
, parameterizes maps from
\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}^{3}}
to an iterated extension of
\mathcal{O}_{\textup{pt}}
together with a fixed underlying iterated extension of
\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{x}}
,
\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{y}}
, and
\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{z}}
.

Indeed, we conjecture that for appropriate stability conditions and framing structure, the fixed points of the resulting moduli space are indexed by the set of plane partitions with fixed asymptotics
\alpha,\beta,\gamma
, where each of the partitions is determined by the framing structure at the framing vertex
i
, given by the pair
A^{i}_{1},A^{i}_{2}
of fixed endomorphisms of
V_{\infty}^{i}
, for
i=x,y,z
respectively. As we will see, this is closely related to their occurrence in the construction of
[
FJMM12
]
.

Example 4.50
.

Similarly, we can also consider the analogous computation in the setting of Example
4.41
, taking

M=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}_{xy}^{2}}[1]\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}_{xz}^{2}}[1]\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}_{yz}^{2}}[1]\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}_{x}}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{y}}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{z}}\ ,

and again using the
t
-structure of Example
4.13
. In particular, the framing vertex has six components

V_{\infty}=V_{\infty}^{xy}\oplus V_{\infty}^{xz}\oplus V_{\infty}^{yz}\oplus V_{\infty}^{x}\oplus V_{\infty}^{y}\oplus V_{\infty}^{z}\,

corresponding to the summands of
M
