which we have drawn in the case
V_{\infty}^{xz}=V_{\infty}^{xz}=V_{\infty}^{z}=0
, for simplicity.

Again, in this example the moduli stack of framed perverse coherent extensions parameterizes, rather than just maps from a fixed iterated extension of
\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}^{2}}
to an iterated extension of
\mathcal{O}_{\textup{pt}}
, maps from the same source to an iterated extension of
\mathcal{O}_{\textup{pt}}
together with a fixed underlying iterated extension of
\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{x}}
,
\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{y}}
, and
\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{z}}
, determined by the framing structure.

Indeed, generalizing the previous example, we conjecture that for appropriate stability conditions, the fixed points of the resulting moduli space are indexed by the set of plane partitions with fixed asymptotics
\alpha,\beta,\gamma
, and a pit at location
(m,n)
, in the sense of
[
BFM15
]
, where the partitions
\alpha,\beta,\gamma
are those of length
\dim V_{\infty}^{i}
determined by the pair
A^{i}_{1},A^{i}_{2}
of endomorphisms of
V_{\infty}^{i}
given by the framing structure at the framing vertex
i
, for
i=x,y,z
respectively,
\dim V_{\infty}^{xz}=m
,
\dim V_{\infty}^{yz}=n
, and
V_{\infty}^{xy}=0
, and
A^{xz}
and
A^{yz}
are given by principal nilpotents in
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m}
and
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{n}
, respectively. For
n=0
, these appear to be the cohomological variants of the modules constructed in
[
FFJ+11
]
.

5.
Representations of cohomological Hall algebras from perverse coherent extensions

5.1.
Overview of Section
5

In Section
5
, we recall the construction of the Kontsevich-Soibelman cohomological Hall algebra from
[
KS11a
]
, and prove Theorem
B
from the introduction, following the approach of
[
Soi16
]
. In Section
5.2
we recall some necessary facts about sheaves of vanishing cycles, and in Section
5.3
we recall the construction of the cohomological Hall algebra. In Section
5.4
we prove Theorem
B
, and in Section
5.5
we explain the interpretation of the vector spaces underlying these representations as cohomological enumerative invariants. In Section
5.6
, we outline an extension of the construction of the representation of Theorem
B
to a representation of a larger algebra which appears to agree with the shifted quiver Yangian of
[
GLY21
]
.

5.2.
Vanishing cycles sheaves and cohomology

In this section, we review the formalism of nearby and vanishing cycles, and recall some of their key properties that we use in section.

Let
X
be a smooth variety,
W:X\to\mathbb{A}^{1}
a regular function, and
X_{0}=X\times_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}\{0\}
,
U=X\times_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}\mathbb{G}_{m}
,
\tilde{\mathbb{G}}_{m}
the universal cover of
\mathbb{G}_{m}
, and
\tilde{U}=U\times_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}\tilde{\mathbb{G}}_{m}
, so we have that

(5.1)

\textstyle{X_{0}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{\iota_{0}}
\textstyle{X\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{W}
\textstyle{U\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{j}
\textstyle{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\tilde{U}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{\tilde{\pi}}
\textstyle{\{0\}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\textstyle{\mathbb{A}^{1}}
\textstyle{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\mathbb{G}_{m}}
\textstyle{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\tilde{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}
,

is commutative, with all squares Cartesian. The nearby cycles functor is defined as

\psi_{W}:=\iota_{0}^{*}j_{*}\tilde{\pi}_{*}\tilde{\pi}^{*}:{\textup{D}_{c}}(U)\to{\textup{D}_{c}}(X_{0})\ .

Note that the unit of the
(\pi^{*},\pi_{*})
adjunction for
\pi=j\circ\tilde{\pi}:\tilde{U}\to X
defines a natural transformation

\iota^{*}A\to\psi_{W}j^{*}A

the cone on which extends to define the vanishing cycles functor

\phi_{W,0}:{\textup{D}_{c}}(X)\to{\textup{D}_{c}}(X_{0})\quad\quad\quad\quad A\mapsto\phi_{W,0}(A)\cong\textup{Cone}\left[\iota^{*}A\to\psi_{W}j^{*}A\right]\ .

In fact, it is convenient to consider the cohomological shifts
\psi_{W}^{p}=\psi_{W}[-1],\phi_{W,0}^{p}=\phi_{W,0}[-1]
as these both preserve the hearts of the respective perverse t-structures, that is, they restrict to functors

\psi_{W}^{p,0}:\textup{Perv}(U)\to\textup{Perv}(X_{0})\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad\phi_{W,0}^{p,0}:\textup{Perv}(X)\to\textup{Perv}(X_{0})\ .

Let
Z=\textup{Crit}(W):=\Gamma_{dW}\times_{T^{\vee}X}X\to X
denote the (classical) critical locus of
W
, that is, the (classical) vanishing locus of
dW\in\Omega^{1}(X)
. Note
W
is constant on each of the finitely many irreducible components of
Z
, so that
f(Z)\subset\mathbb{A}^{1}
is a finite set of points, and we have

Z=\bigsqcup_{c\in f(Z)}Z_{c}\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad Z_{c}=Z\times_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}\{c\}

so that we have the following commutative diagram, with all squares Cartesian:

\textstyle{Z_{c}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{i_{c}}
\textstyle{X_{c}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{\iota_{c}}
\textstyle{\{c\}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\textstyle{Z\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{i}
\textstyle{X\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{W}
\textstyle{\mathbb{A}^{1}}
.

For each
c\in W(Z)\subset\mathbb{A}^{1}
, we consider the corresponding shifted vanishing cycles functor for the function
W-c
, denoted
\phi_{W,c}^{p}:=\phi_{W-c,0}^{p}:{\textup{D}}(X)\to{\textup{D}}(X_{c})
, and define

\phi_{W,c}^{p,0}:\textup{Perv}(X)\to\textup{Perv}(X_{c})\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad\varphi_{W,c}=\phi_{W,c}^{p,0}(\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X}[\dim X])\ \in\textup{Perv}(X_{c})\ .

In fact, the support of
\varphi_{W,c}
is contained in
Z_{c}\subset X_{c}
, and thus we also define the internal variant of the
c
component of the vanishing cycle sheaf

\tilde{\varphi}_{W,c}=i_{c}^{*}\varphi_{W,c}\in\textup{Perv}(Z_{c})

as the image of
\varphi_{W,c}
under the equivalence
\textup{Perv}(X_{c})_{Z_{c}}\cong\textup{Perv}(Z_{c})
. Finally, we define the total intrinsic variant of the vanishing cycle sheaf

\tilde{\varphi}_{W}:=\bigoplus_{c\in W(Z)}\tilde{\varphi}_{W,c}\quad\in\quad\textup{Perv}(Z)=\bigoplus_{c\in W(Z)}\textup{Perv}(Z_{c})\ ,

and similarly its extrinsic analogue, which will be the primary object of interest

\varphi_{W}:=\iota_{*}\tilde{\varphi}_{W}\ \in\textup{PervCoh}(X)\ .

More generally, we define the total extrinsic vanishing cycles functor

\phi_{W}=\bigoplus_{c\in W(Z)}\iota_{c*}\circ\phi^{p}_{W,c}:{\textup{D}}(X)\to{\textup{D}}(X)\ ,

which in particular reproduces the preceding object as
\varphi_{W}=\phi_{W}(\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X}[\dim X])
.

We define the compactly supported vanishing cycles cohomology of
X
, and its perverse shifted analogue, by

H^{\bullet}_{c}(X,\phi_{W}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X})=p_{!}\phi_{W}p^{*}\mathbb{Q}\quad\quad\quad\quad H^{\bullet}_{c}(X,\varphi_{W})=p_{!}\phi_{W}p^{*}\mathbb{Q}[\dim X]\ ,

where
p:X\to\textup{pt}
. It satisfies the following functoriality properties:

Proposition 5.1
.

Let
W:Y\to\mathbb{A}^{1}
and
f:X\to Y
a proper map of smooth varieties. Then
f
induces a pullback map

(5.2)

f^{*}:H_{c}^{\bullet}(Y,\phi_{W}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{Y})\to H^{\bullet}_{c}(X,\phi_{W\circ f}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X})\ .

Similarly, a smooth map
f:X\to Y
of smooth varieties induces a pushforward map

(5.3)

f_{*}:H^{\bullet}_{c}(X,\phi_{W\circ f}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X})\to H_{c}^{\bullet}(Y,\phi_{W}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{Y})[-2d]\ ,

where
d=\dim X-\dim Y
denotes the relative dimension of
f
.

Proof.

Recall that for any map of smooth varieties, there is a natural transformation

\phi_{W}\xrightarrow{}f_{*}\phi_{W\circ f}f^{*}\ ;

see for example Equation 20 in
[
Dav17
]
. This induces the desired map as

p_{Y!}\phi_{W}p_{Y}^{*}\mathbb{Q}\to p_{Y!}f_{*}\phi_{W\circ f}f^{*}p_{Y}^{*}\mathbb{Q}\cong p_{X!}\phi_{W\circ f}p_{X}^{*}\mathbb{Q}\ ,

where we have used properness of
f
to identify
f_{*}=f_{!}
.

Similarly, for
f
a smooth map of smooth varieties, the induced natural transformation

f^{*}\phi_{W}\xrightarrow{\cong}\phi_{W\circ f}f^{*}

is an isomorphism; see for example Equation 23 in
loc. cit.
. This induces the desired map as

p_{X!}\phi_{W\circ f}p_{X}^{*}\mathbb{Q}\cong p_{Y!}f_{!}\phi_{W\circ f}f^{*}p_{Y}^{*}\mathbb{Q}\xrightarrow{\cong}p_{Y!}f_{!}f^{*}\phi_{W}p_{Y}^{*}\mathbb{Q}\to p_{Y!}\phi_{W}p_{Y}^{*}\mathbb{Q}[-2d]

where we have used the counit
f_{!}f^{!}\to{\textup{id}}
of the
(f_{!},f^{!})
adjunction, as well as the identification
f^{*}=f^{!}[-2d]
which follows from smoothness of
f
.
∎

In particular, we also obtain:

Corollary 5.2
.

For
f:X\to Y
an affine fibration of relative dimension
d
, the induced pushforward map of Equation
5.3
is an isomorphism, so that there is an inverse isomorphism

(5.4)

f_{*}^{-1}:H_{c}^{\bullet}(Y,\phi_{W}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{Y})\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{\bullet}_{c}(X,\phi_{W\circ f}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X})[2d]\ .

Proof.

If
f
is an affine fibration, the counit of the
(f_{!},f^{!})
adjunction is an isomorphism, and thus by the proof of the preceding proposition the induced map is an isomorphism.
∎

5.3.
Cohomological Hall algebras of quivers with potential and Calabi-Yau threefolds

Throughout this section, let
(Q,W)
be a quiver with potential, and recall from Section
3.6
the moduli stacks of representations of the underlying quiver

\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}(Q)=[X_{\textbf{d}}(Q)/G_{\textbf{d}}(Q)]\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad X_{\textbf{d}}(Q)=\prod_{e\in E_{Q}}\Hom({\mathbb{K}}^{d_{s(e)}},{\mathbb{K}}^{d_{t(e)}})\quad\quad G_{\textbf{d}}(Q)=\prod_{i\in V_{Q}}{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{i}}({\mathbb{K}})

for each dimension vector
{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}
; for simplicity, we will often omit
Q
from the notation when there is only a single quiver under consideration, as in the remainder of this subsection.

Given
{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}
, we define

\mathfrak{M}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}=[X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}]\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad\begin{cases}X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}=\big\{\varphi\in X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}\ \big|\ \varphi\big(\bigoplus_{e\in E_{Q}}\mathbb{K}^{a_{s(e)}}\big)\subset\bigoplus_{e\in E_{Q}}\mathbb{K}^{a_{t(e)}}\big\}\\
G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}=\big\{g\in G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}\ \big|\ g\big(\bigoplus_{i\in V_{Q}}{\mathbb{K}}^{a_{i}}\big)\subset\bigoplus_{i\in V_{Q}}{\mathbb{K}}^{a_{i}+b_{i}}\big\}\ .\end{cases}

Equivalently, these spaces are defined component-wise as

X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}=\prod_{e\in E_{Q}}\Hom_{a_{s(e)},a_{t(e)}}({\mathbb{K}}^{a_{s(e)}+b_{s(e)}},{\mathbb{K}}^{a_{t(e)}+b_{t(e)}})\quad\quad\textup{and}\quad\quad G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}=\prod_{i\in V_{Q}}{\textup{Gl}}_{a_{i},b_{i}}({\mathbb{K}})

where
\Hom_{m_{1},m_{2}}({\mathbb{K}}^{m_{1}+n_{1}},{\mathbb{K}}^{m_{2}+n_{2}})
denotes the space of block upper triangular linear maps, that is, satisfying
\varphi({\mathbb{K}}^{m_{1}})\subset{\mathbb{K}}^{m_{2}}
, and
{\textup{Gl}}_{m,n}({\mathbb{K}})\subset{\textup{Gl}}_{m+n}({\mathbb{K}})
is the parabolic subgroup preserving the flag
\{0\}\subset{\mathbb{K}}^{m}\subset{\mathbb{K}}^{m+n}
.

Geometrically,
\mathfrak{M}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}
is the moduli stack of short exact sequences of representations of the quiver
Q
with sub object and quotient object of dimension
a
and
b
, respectively. In particular, note that we have a closed embedding
X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}\to X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}
by definition, as well as a smooth map
X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}\to X_{\textbf{a}}\times X_{\textbf{b}}
given by forgetting the extension data. These maps define a correspondence of algebraic
\mathbb{K}
-stacks

\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 21.27258pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\cr&&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-3.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{}$}}}}}}}{\hbox{\kern 45.27258pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{M}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 13.80008pt\raise-24.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 99.78891pt\raise-24.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}{\hbox{\kern-21.27258pt\raise-31.33331pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{M}_{{\textbf{a}}}\times\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{b}}}$}}}}}}}{\hbox{\kern 55.95488pt\raise-31.33331pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{}$}}}}}}}{\hbox{\kern 96.63718pt\raise-31.33331pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{M}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\ ,

inducing an associative product on the Borel-Moore homology of
\mathfrak{M}
with coefficients in the sheaf of vanishing cycles determined by
W
, as we now explain.

We recall the definition of the cohomological Hall algebra associated to the quiver with potential
(Q,W)
following
[
KS11a
]
. The underlying graded vector space is given by

\mathcal{H}(Q,W)=\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}\mathcal{H}_{\textbf{d}}(Q,W)\quad\quad\mathcal{H}_{\textbf{d}}(Q,W)=H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}(Q)}(X_{\textbf{d}}(Q),\varphi_{W_{\textbf{d}}})

where
H_{\bullet}^{G}(X,\varphi):=H^{\bullet}_{G,c}(X,\varphi)^{\vee}
denotes the equivariant Borel-Moore homology with coefficients in the sheaf of vanishing cycles, defined as the dual of the compactly supported cohomology with coefficients in the sheaf of vanishing cycles, and we recall that the natural perverse grading shift in the equivariant case is given by

H^{\bullet}_{G,c}(X,\varphi)=H^{\bullet}_{G,c}(X,\phi_{W}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X})[\dim X-\dim G]\ .

Again, for simplicity, we will often omit
(Q,W)
from the notation when there is only a single quiver with potential under consideration.

The cohomological Hall algebra is not a graded algebra in the usual sense: rather than being an associative algebra object internal to the category
\Vect_{\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}
of
\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}
-graded complexes with its usual monoidal structure, it is an associative algebra in this category with respect to the usual monoidal structure twisted by a cohomological degree shift, defined by

(\bigoplus_{{\textbf{a}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}V_{\textbf{a}})\otimes^{\textup{tw}}(\bigoplus_{{\textbf{b}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}W_{\textbf{b}}):=\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}\bigoplus_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}={\textbf{d}}}V_{\textbf{a}}\otimes W_{\textbf{b}}[\chi({\textbf{b}},{\textbf{a}})-\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})]\ ,

as explained in Section 2.7 of
[
KS11a
]
or 3.1 of
[
Dav17
]
, where we have used the bilinear form
\chi:\mathbb{Z}^{V_{Q}}\times\mathbb{Z}^{V_{Q}}\to\mathbb{Z}
defined by

\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})=\sum_{i\in V_{Q}}a_{i}b_{i}-\sum_{e\in E_{Q}}a_{s(e)}b_{t(e)}\ .

In particular, note that
\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{a}})=\dim G_{\textbf{a}}-\dim X_{\textbf{a}}
and similarly

(5.5)

\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})=\dim G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}-\dim G_{\textbf{a}}\times G_{\textbf{b}}-\dim X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}+\dim X_{{\textbf{a}}}\times X_{\textbf{b}}\ .

We now recall the construction of the cohomological Hall algebra of a quiver with potential introduced by Kontsevich-Soibelman in
[
KS11a
]
.

Theorem 5.3
.

[
KS11a
]
Let
(Q,W)
be a quiver with potential. The Kontsevich-Soibelman cohomological Hall algebra

\mathcal{H}(Q,W)\in\textup{Alg}_{\textup{Ass}}(\Vect_{\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}^{\otimes^{\textup{tw}}})\ ,

that is,
\mathcal{H}(Q,W)
admits a canonical (twisted
\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}
-graded) associative algebra structure.

Proof.

The associative product map
m:\mathcal{H}\otimes^{\textup{tw}}\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}
on the cohomological Hall algebra
\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}(Q,W)
is defined in components by

m_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}:\mathcal{H}_{\textbf{a}}\otimes\mathcal{H}_{\textbf{b}}\to\mathcal{H}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}[\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})-\chi({\textbf{b}},{\textbf{a}})]\ .

The components
m_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}
will be constructed in terms of the equivalent dual maps

m_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{\vee}:H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},\varphi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{a}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}},\varphi_{W_{\textbf{a}}})\otimes H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X_{{\textbf{b}}},\varphi_{W_{\textbf{b}}})[\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})-\chi({\textbf{b}},{\textbf{a}})]\ ,

or after accounting explicitly for the perverse shifts,

(5.6)

m_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{\vee}:H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{a}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{\textbf{a}}})\otimes H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X_{{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{\textbf{b}}})[2\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})]\ ,

where the claimed cohomological degree shift follows from the equality

\chi({\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}},{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}})-\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{a}})-\chi({\textbf{b}},{\textbf{b}})+\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})-\chi({\textbf{b}},{\textbf{a}})=2\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})\ .

We now proceed with the construction of the desired maps:

There is a restriction of equivariance map

H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}})

given by the proper pullback map of Equation
5.2
induced by the map

X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}\to X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}

which is proper and schematic, as its fibres are isomorphic to the partial flag variety
G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}
. Similarly, pullback along the closed embedding
X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}\to X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}
gives a map

H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}})\ .

Next, there is a further restriction of equivariance map

H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}}\times G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}})[2(\dim G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}-\dim G_{\textbf{a}}\times G_{\textbf{b}})]

given by the inverse pushforward map, as in Equation
5.4
, induced by the affine fibration

X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}/(G_{\textbf{a}}\times G_{\textbf{b}})\to X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}

with fibres given by the unipotent group
G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}/(G_{\textbf{a}}\times G_{\textbf{b}})
. There is also a pushforward map

H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}}\times G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}}\times G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}}\times X_{\textbf{b}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}}\boxtimes W_{\textbf{b}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}}}\times X_{\textbf{b}}})[-2(\dim X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}-\dim X_{\textbf{a}}\times X_{\textbf{b}})]

induced as in Equation
5.3
by the smooth map

X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}/(G_{\textbf{a}}\times G_{\textbf{b}})\to(X_{{\textbf{a}}}\times X_{\textbf{b}})/(G_{\textbf{a}}\times G_{\textbf{b}})\ .

Composing the above sequence of maps with the Thom-Sebastiani isomorphism

H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}}\times G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}}\times X_{\textbf{b}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}}\boxtimes W_{\textbf{b}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}}}\times X_{\textbf{b}}})\cong H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{a}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{\textbf{a}}})\otimes H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X_{{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{\textbf{b}}})\ ,

gives the desired map of Equation
5.6
, where the correct shift follows from the equality of Equation
5.5
. Associativity of the above product follows from a standard argument; see for example Section 2.3 of
[
KS11a
]
.

∎

In particular, we make the following definition:

Definition 5.4
.

Let
Y\xrightarrow{\pi}X
be a resolution of singularities of a toric Calabi-Yau threefold satisfying the hypotheses of Section
3.2
. The cohomological Hall algebra of
Y
is defined by

\mathcal{H}(Y):=\mathcal{H}(Q_{Y},W_{Y})\ \in\textup{Alg}_{\textup{Ass}}(\Vect_{\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}^{\otimes^{\textup{tw}}})\ ,

as constructed in the preceding Proposition, where
(Q_{Y},W_{Y})
is the quiver with potential associated to
Y
as in Theorem
3.32
.

5.4.
Representations of cohomological Hall algebras from perverse coherent extensions

In this section, we prove Theorem
B
from Section
1.2
of the introduction, following the results outlined in Section 4 of
[
Soi16
]
.

Let
M\in\textup{PervCoh}^{\textup{p}}(Y)^{T}
satisfy the hypotheses of Section
4.1
with
Q_{M}
be the associated extended quiver, and let
f
be a framing structure for
M
of rank
d_{\infty}
with
(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
the associated framed quiver with potential, as in Theorem
4.38
. Recall that by the construction in
loc. cit.
we have

X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}})=\bigoplus_{i,j\in V_{Q}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma^{1}_{j}\otimes\Hom(\mathbb{K}^{d_{i}},\mathbb{K}^{d_{j}})\oplus\bigoplus_{i\in V_{Q}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}\otimes\Hom(\mathbb{K}^{d_{i}},\mathbb{K}^{d_{\infty}})\oplus\bigoplus_{j\in V_{Q}}\ {}_{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{j}\otimes\Hom(\mathbb{K}^{d_{\infty}},\mathbb{K}^{d_{j}})

for each
{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}
, as well as the closed subvariety

Z_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}})=\textup{Crit}(W^{\textup{f}}_{M,{\textbf{d}}})\subset X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}})\quad\quad\text{invariant under}\quad\quad G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{Y})=\prod_{i\in V_{Q_{Y}}}{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{i}}(\mathbb{K})\ .

Throughout this section, we will drop the dependence on the choice of quiver
Q_{Y}
and extended quiver
Q_{M}
from the notation, and write simply

X^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}=X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}})\quad\quad X_{\textbf{d}}=X_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{Y})\quad\quad\textup{and}\quad\quad G_{\textbf{d}}=G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{Y})\ .

Further, we fix a choice of stability condition
\zeta\in\mathbb{R}^{V_{Q}}
for the framed quiver with potential
(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
and let
X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}\subset X^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{d}}
denote the open subvariety of
\zeta
-stable points.

As in the preceding Section
5.3
, for
{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}
, we let
{\textbf{a}}^{0}=({\textbf{a}},0),{\textbf{b}}^{\textup{f}}=({\textbf{b}},d_{\infty})\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}}}
and define

\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}=[X^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}]\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad\begin{cases}X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{\textup{f}}=\big\{\varphi\in X^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}\ \big|\ \varphi\big(\bigoplus_{e\in E_{Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}}}\mathbb{K}^{a^{0}_{s(e)}}\big)\subset\bigoplus_{e\in E_{Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}}}\mathbb{K}^{a^{0}_{t(e)}}\big\}\\
G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}=\big\{g\in G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}\ \big|\ g\big(\bigoplus_{i\in V_{Q_{Y}}}{\mathbb{K}}^{a_{i}}\big)\subset\bigoplus_{i\in V_{Q_{Y}}}{\mathbb{K}}^{a_{i}}\big\}\end{cases}\ .

Equivalently, these spaces are defined component-wise as

X^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}=\prod_{e\in E_{Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}}}\Hom_{a^{0}_{s(e)},a^{0}_{t(e)}}({\mathbb{K}}^{a^{0}_{s(e)}+b^{\textup{f}}_{s(e)}},{\mathbb{K}}^{a^{0}_{t(e)}+b^{\textup{f}}_{t(e)}})\quad\quad\textup{and}\quad\quad G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}=\prod_{i\in V_{Q_{Y}}}{\textup{Gl}}_{a_{i},b_{i}}({\mathbb{K}})

where
\Hom_{m_{1},m_{2}}({\mathbb{K}}^{m_{1}+n_{1}},{\mathbb{K}}^{m_{2}+n_{2}})
denotes the space of block upper triangular linear maps, that is, satisfying
\varphi({\mathbb{K}}^{m_{1}})\subset{\mathbb{K}}^{m_{2}}
, and
{\textup{Gl}}_{m,n}({\mathbb{K}})\subset{\textup{Gl}}_{m+n}({\mathbb{K}})
is the parabolic subgroup preserving the flag
\{0\}\subset{\mathbb{K}}^{m}\subset{\mathbb{K}}^{m+n}
.

Geometrically,
\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}
is the moduli stack of short exact sequences of representations of the framed quiver
Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}
with sub object and quotient object of dimension
{\textbf{a}}^{0}
and
{\textbf{b}}^{\textup{f}}
, respectively. Note that since the sub object has framing dimension
0
and thus is equivalent to a representation of the unframed quiver
Q_{Y}
. In particular, note that we again have a closed embedding
X^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}\to X^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}
by definition, as well as a smooth map
X^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}\to X_{\textbf{a}}\times X^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{b}}
given by forgetting the extension data. These maps define a correspondence of algebraic
\mathbb{K}
-stacks

\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 21.27258pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\cr&&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-3.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{}$}}}}}}}{\hbox{\kern 45.27258pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 16.06615pt\raise-24.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 97.74477pt\raise-24.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}{\hbox{\kern-21.27258pt\raise-32.99002pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{M}_{{\textbf{a}}}\times\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{b}}}$}}}}}}}{\hbox{\kern 55.95488pt\raise-32.99002pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{}$}}}}}}}{\hbox{\kern 96.63718pt\raise-32.99002pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{M}^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\ .

Analogously to the previous section, this correspondence will induce the desired module structure on the Borel-Moore homology of
\mathfrak{M}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}
with coefficients in the sheaf of vanishing cycles determined by
W^{\textup{f}}
, but we must modify the correspondence to ensure it preserves the moduli spaces of
\zeta
-stable representations.

We define subschemes
X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{\textbf{b}}},X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}},X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}\subset X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{\textup{f}}
by requiring that the diagrams

\textstyle{X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{\textbf{b}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\textstyle{X_{\textbf{b}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\textstyle{X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{\textup{f}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\textstyle{X^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{b}}}

\textstyle{X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}

\textstyle{X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{\textup{f}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\textstyle{X^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}

\textstyle{X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}

are Cartesian. Note that the subschemes

are all open, by base change, and we have that

. Similarly, the maps

are smooth and a closed embedding, respectively, by base change. In order to complete the construction, we will need to make an additional hypothesis on the stability condition

:

Definition 5.5
.

A stability condition
\zeta
is called
compatible
with
M
if the composition

[X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}]\to[X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}]\to[X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}]

is proper for each
{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}
.

We now construct the desired representations
{\mathbb{V}}={\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}(M)
defined by an object
M\in{\textup{D}}^{b}\textup{Coh}(Y)^{T}
together with a choice of framing structure

and a compatible stability condition

. The underlying graded vector space is given by

{\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}(M)=\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}{\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(M)\quad\quad\text{with}\quad\quad{\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(M)=H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}(Q)}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}),\varphi_{W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}}})\ ,

where we recall that
H_{\bullet}^{G}(X,\varphi):=H^{\bullet}_{G,c}(X,\varphi)^{\vee}
denotes the equivariant Borel-Moore homology with coefficients in the sheaf of vanishing cycles, defined as the dual of the compactly supported cohomology with coefficients in the sheaf of vanishing cycles, as in Section
5.3
. The main result of this section is the following, which closely follows the proof of Theorem
5.3
above from
[
KS11a
]
:

Let
Y\to X
be as in Section
3.2
,
M\in{\textup{D}}^{b}\textup{Coh}(Y)^{T}
satisfy the hypotheses of Sections
4.1
and
4.6
,
{\textup{f}}\in Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{M},R_{M})(\mathbb{K})
be a framing structure on
M
, and
\zeta
a compatible stability condition. Then we have the following result, which establishes Theorem
B
from the introduction:

Theorem 5.6
.

There exists a natural (twisted
\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}
-graded) representation

\rho_{M}:\mathcal{H}(Y)\to{\textup{End}}_{\Vect_{\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}}({\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}(M))

of the cohomological Hall algebra
\mathcal{H}(Y)
on
{\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}(M)
.

Proof.

The module structure map
\rho:\mathcal{H}\otimes^{\textup{tw}}{\mathbb{V}}\to{\mathbb{V}}
for
{\mathbb{V}}={\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}(M)
over the cohomological Hall algebra
\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}(Y)
is defined in components by

\rho_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}:\mathcal{H}_{\textbf{a}}\otimes{\mathbb{V}}_{\textbf{b}}\to{\mathbb{V}}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}[\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})-\chi({\textbf{b}},{\textbf{a}})]\ .

The components
\rho_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}
will be constructed in terms of the equivalent dual maps

\rho_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{\vee}:H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},\varphi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{a}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}},\varphi_{W_{\textbf{a}}})\otimes H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{b}}},\varphi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{b}}})[\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})-\chi({\textbf{b}},{\textbf{a}})]\ ,

or after accounting explicitly for the perverse shifts,

(5.7)

\rho_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{\vee}:H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{a}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{\textbf{a}}})\otimes H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{b}}})[2\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})]\ ,

where the claimed cohomological degree shift again follows from the equality

\chi({\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}},{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}})-\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{a}})-\chi({\textbf{b}},{\textbf{b}})+\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})-\chi({\textbf{b}},{\textbf{a}})=2\chi({\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}})\ .

We now proceed with the construction of the desired maps:

There is again a restriction of equivariance map

H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}})

given by the proper pullback map of Equation
5.2
induced by the map

X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}\to X_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}

which is proper and schematic, as its fibres are isomorphic to the partial flag variety
G_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}
. Similarly, pullback along the map
[X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}]\to[X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}]
, which is proper by the compatibility of
\zeta
, gives a map

H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}}+{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}})\ .

Next, there is again a further restriction of equivariance map

H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}}\times G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}})[2(\dim G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}-\dim G_{\textbf{a}}\times G_{\textbf{b}})]

given by the inverse pushforward map, as in Equation
5.4
, induced by the affine fibration

X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}/(G_{\textbf{a}}\times G_{\textbf{b}})\to X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}/G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}

with fibres given by the unipotent group
G_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}/(G_{\textbf{a}}\times G_{\textbf{b}})
.

There is also a pushforward map

H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}}\times G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}}\times G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{\textbf{b}}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{\textbf{b}}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}})

induced as in Equation
5.3
by the map
X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}\to X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{\textbf{b}}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}
since it is an open immersion and thus smooth. Similarly, there is again a pushforward map

H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}}\times G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{\textbf{b}}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}})\to H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}}\times G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}}\times X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{b}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}}\boxtimes W^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{b}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}}}\times X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{\textbf{b}}}_{\textbf{b}}})[-2(\dim X^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}-\dim X_{\textbf{a}}\times X^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{b}})]

induced by the smooth map

X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta_{\textbf{b}}}_{{\textbf{a}},{\textbf{b}}}/(G_{\textbf{a}}\times G_{\textbf{b}})\to(X_{{\textbf{a}}}\times X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{b}})/(G_{\textbf{a}}\times G_{\textbf{b}})\ .

Composing the above sequence of maps with the Thom-Sebastiani isomorphism

H^{\bullet}_{G_{{\textbf{a}}}\times G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}}\times X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{b}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}}\boxtimes W^{\textup{f}}_{\textbf{b}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{{\textbf{a}}}\times X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{b}}})\cong H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{a}},c}(X_{{\textbf{a}}},\phi_{W_{{\textbf{a}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X_{\textbf{a}}})\otimes H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{b}},c}(X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{{\textbf{b}}},\phi_{W^{\textup{f}}_{{\textbf{b}}}}\underline{\mathbb{Q}}_{X^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{b}}})\ ,

gives the desired map of Equation
5.7
, where the correct shift follows from the equality of Equation
5.5
. Commutativity of the diagram

\textstyle{\mathcal{H}\otimes^{\textup{tw}}\mathcal{H}\otimes^{\textup{tw}}{\mathbb{V}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{{\textup{id}}_{\mathcal{H}}\otimes\rho}
\scriptstyle{m_{\mathcal{H}}\otimes{\textup{id}}_{{\mathbb{V}}}}
\textstyle{\mathcal{H}\otimes^{\textup{tw}}{\mathbb{V}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{\rho}
\textstyle{\mathcal{H}\otimes^{\textup{tw}}{\mathbb{V}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{\rho}
\textstyle{\mathbb{V}}

follows from a standard argument, similar to that of the associativity of the product on the cohomological Hall algebra; see for example Section 2.3 of
[
KS11a
]
.
∎

5.5.
Enumerative invariants from perverse coherent extensions

The vector spaces
\mathbb{V}_{M}^{\zeta}(Y)
underlying the modules constructed in the preceding section should be understood as a family of categorified enumerative invariants of the threefold
Y
, which are heuristically given by counting the number of
\zeta
-stable iterated extensions of the object
M
with compactly supported perverse coherent sheaves. We now formally define the corresponding enumerative invariants and recall their relation with geometry, which follow from the seminal results of
[
Beh09
]
and
[
BF08
]
.

Let
M\in\textup{PervCoh}^{\textup{p}}(Y)^{T}
,
f
a framing structure for
M
of rank
d_{\infty}
, and
(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
the associated framed quiver with potential, and
\zeta
a stability condition on
X^{\textup{f}}(Q_{M})
as in the preceding section, and recall that the graded vector space underlying
\mathbb{V}_{M}^{\zeta}(Y)
is given by

{\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}(M)=\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}{\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(M)\quad\quad\text{with}\quad\quad{\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(M)=H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}(Q)}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}),\varphi_{W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}}})\ .

We define the generating functional for the corresponding enumerative invariants by

(5.8)

{\mathcal{Z}}_{M}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}({{\textbf{q}}})=\sum_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}{{\textbf{q}}}^{\textbf{d}}\chi(\mathbb{V}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(M))\quad\in{{\mathbb{Z}[\![{{\textbf{q}}}]\!]}}\ ,

where we introduce the shorthand notation
{{\textbf{q}}}^{\textbf{d}}=\prod_{i\in V_{Q_{Y}}}q_{i}^{d_{i}}
and
{{\mathbb{Z}[\![{{\textbf{q}}}]\!]}}=\mathbb{Z}[\![q_{i}]\!]_{i\in V_{Q_{Y}}}
, and
\chi
denotes the Euler characteristic of the cohomologically graded vector space.

Now, suppose that the stability condition
\zeta
is chosen so that there are no strictly semi-stable points and
\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}})=X^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}})/G_{\textbf{d}}(Q)
is a smooth scheme for each
{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}
, so that the function
W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{\textup{f}}:X^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}})\to\mathbb{K}
descends to a regular function
\overline{W}_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{\textup{f}}:\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}})\to\mathbb{K}
, and we have that

\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})=\left[\textup{Crit}(W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{\textup{f}}|_{X_{{\textbf{d}}}^{\zeta}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}})})/G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{Y})\right]=\textup{Crit}(\overline{W}_{M}^{\textup{f}})\subset\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}})\ ,

that is, the moduli space
\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
of
\zeta
-stable representations of the quiver with potential
(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
is a global critical locus of a regular function on a smooth scheme. In particular, we have

(5.9)

{\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(M)=H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}(Q)}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}),\varphi_{W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}}})=H_{\bullet}(\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}}),\varphi_{\overline{W}_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{\textup{f}}})\ .

Moreover, the results of
[
Beh09
]
imply that
\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
admits a symmetric obstruction theory inducing a virtual fundamental class
[\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})]^{\textup{vir}}\in H_{\bullet}(\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}}))
and corresponding invariants

\tilde{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{M}({{\textbf{q}}})=\sum_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}{{\textbf{q}}}^{\textbf{d}}\int_{[\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})]^{\textup{vir}}}1\quad\in{{\mathbb{Z}[\![{{\textbf{q}}}]\!]}}\ ,

which heuristically count the number of points in
\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
, such that these invariants can be computed as

\int_{[\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})]^{\textup{vir}}}1=\chi(\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}}),\nu_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{\zeta}):=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}n\ \chi((\nu_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{\zeta})^{-1}\{n\})\ ,

the weighted Euler characteristic of
\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
with respect to a constructible function

\nu_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{\zeta}:\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})\to\mathbb{Z}\ .

Moreover, it is shown in
loc. cit.
that in the case of a critical locus, this constructible function can be computed locally in terms of the Euler characteristic of the Milnor fibre of the potential, inducing an identification

\chi(\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}}),\nu_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{\zeta})=\chi({\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(M))\quad\quad\textup{and thus}\quad\quad{\mathcal{Z}}_{M}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}=\tilde{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}_{M}\ .

We now recall some additional hypotheses that allow for a concrete combinatorial approach to calculating these invariants, and which are valid in many examples of interest. Let
\tilde{T}\subset T
denote the maximal torus of
T
which preserves the Calabi-Yau structure on
Y
, and recall that there is a natural action of
T
on
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta,{\textup{f}}}(Q_{M})
induced by the action on the underlying threefold
Y
, such that the subtorus
\tilde{T}
preserves the potential
W_{M}^{\textup{f}}
and thus naturally acts on the moduli space
\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
.

Additionally, let
T_{\textup{f}}
be a maximal torus of
G^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}=\textup{Stab}_{{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(\mathbb{K})}({\textup{f}})
the subgroup of
{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(\mathbb{K})
stabilizing the point
{\textup{f}}\in Z_{d_{\infty}}(Q_{\infty},R_{\infty})
, and let
A=\tilde{T}\times T_{\textup{f}}
which acts naturally on
X_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{f}}(Q_{M})
such that the potential
W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{\textup{f}}
is
A
invariant and this action commutes with that of
G_{\textbf{d}}
. Thus,
A
also acts naturally on
Z_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{f}}(Q_{M},R_{M})
, as well as the quotient stacks
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\textup{f}}(Q_{M})
and
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
, and similarly we obtain actions on
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}(Q_{M})
and
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
if
A
preserves
\zeta
-stability. Throughout the remainder of this section, we make the following hypothesis:

Hypothesis 5.7
.

We assume that the
A
-fixed subvariety
\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})^{A}
is a finite set
{\text{\<p>}}_{\textbf{d}}
of isolated fixed points.

For simplicity of presentation in the following corollary, we also assume that for each
{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}
, the dimensions of the tangent spaces to the
A
fixed points in the component
\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})
are all of the same parity
(-1)^{k_{\textbf{d}}}
for
k_{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}
.

Under the preceding hypotheses, we can compute the above enumerative invariants using the localization results of
[
BF08
]
, so that we obtain:

Corollary 5.8
.

The above generating function is given by

\mathcal{Z}_{M}^{\zeta}({{\textbf{q}}})=\sum_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}{{\textbf{q}}}^{\textbf{d}}(-1)^{k_{\textbf{d}}}\ |\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})^{A}|\quad\in{{\mathbb{Z}[\![{{\textbf{q}}}]\!]}}\ ,

where
|\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{M}^{\textup{f}},W_{M}^{\textup{f}})^{A}|\in\mathbb{Z}
denotes the cardinality of the set of
A
fixed points.

Proof.

Under the given hypotheses, this follows from Theorem 3.4 and Corollaries 3.5 and 3.6 of
loc. cit.
.
∎

In fact, our description of the set of
T
fixed points induced by the equivalence of Equation
4.35
together with Theorem
4.20
gives a natural enumeration of the fixed points in terms of objects in
\textup{filt}(\Sigma_{M})
, or equivalently in the category of twisted objects
H^{0}(\textup{tw}^{0}(\mathcal{A}_{F\oplus M}))
.

5.6.
Towards representations of shifted quiver Yangians

In this section, we outline the construction of an extension of the geometric action of
\mathcal{H}(Y)
on
\mathcal{V}^{\zeta}(M)
to the action of a larger associative algebra, called a shifted quiver Yangian in
[
LY20
,
GLY21
]
, following the approach of
[
RSYZ19
]
and in turn
[
Tsy17
]
,
[
SV13
]
,
[
Var00
]
and
[
Nak00
]
.

Let
F
denote the field of fractions of the polynomial ring

H_{A}^{\bullet}(\textup{pt})=\mathbb{K}[\hbar_{1},\hbar_{2},\hbar_{3},{{\textbf{x}}}]/(\hbar_{1}+\hbar_{2}+\hbar_{3})\ ,

where we recall that
A=\tilde{T}\times T_{\textup{f}}
is the product of
\tilde{T}\subset T
the maximal torus of
T
which preserves the Calabi-Yau structure on
Y
and
T_{\textup{f}}
a maximal torus of
G^{\textup{c}}_{\textup{f}}=\textup{Stab}_{{\textup{Gl}}_{d_{\infty}}(\mathbb{K})}({\textup{f}})
, and we have introduced the identifications
H_{T_{\textup{f}}}(\textup{pt})=\mathbb{K}[{{\textbf{x}}}]:=\mathbb{K}[x_{j}]_{j=1,..,{\textup{rk}}(T_{\textup{f}})}
and
H^{\bullet}_{T}(\textup{pt})=\mathbb{K}[\hbar_{1},\hbar_{2},\hbar_{3}]
such that the Calabi-Yau structure is of weight
(1,1,1)
in the corresponding grading.

Throughout this section, all constructions are given over the base ring
F
by default, though this will be occasionally be suppressed in the notation. In particular, we let

\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}(Q_{Y},W_{Y})^{A}\in\textup{Alg}_{\textup{Ass}}(\Vect_{F,\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}^{\otimes^{\textup{tw}}})\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad{\mathbb{V}}^{\zeta}={\mathbb{V}}^{\zeta}(M)^{A}\in\mathcal{H}{\textup{-Mod}}(\Vect_{F,\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}}^{\otimes^{\textup{tw}}})

denote the localized,
A
-equivariant analogues of the objects introduced under this notation in sections
5.3
and
5.4
, respectively. In particular, for each
{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}
the underlying vector spaces of the degree
d
components are given by

\mathcal{H}_{\textbf{d}}=H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}},\varphi_{W_{\textbf{d}}})\otimes_{H^{\bullet}_{A}(\textup{pt})}F\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad{\mathbb{V}}_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}=H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta},\varphi_{W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}}})\otimes_{H^{\bullet}_{A}(\textup{pt})}F\ .

We define the universal Cartan algebra
\mathcal{H}^{0}
as the polynomial algebra

\mathcal{H}^{0}=\mathcal{H}^{0}(Y)=F[\phi_{n}^{i}]^{i\in I}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\quad\quad\textup{and let}\quad\quad\phi^{i}(z)=1+\sigma_{3}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\phi^{i}_{n}z^{-n-1}\ \in\mathcal{H}^{0}{[\![}z^{-1}{]\!]}\

be a formal generating functional for the variables
\phi_{n}^{i}
, which we will use as a shorthand to write equations involving these variables.

Recall that the analogue of the Chern polynomial in this setting defines a map

c_{1/z}:K_{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta})\to{\textup{End}}_{H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(\textup{pt})}(H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta},\varphi_{W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}}})\otimes_{H^{\bullet}_{A}(\textup{pt})}F){[\![}z^{-1}{]\!]}\ ;

it can be defined for example on vector bundles
E\in K_{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta})
by

c_{1/z}(E)=\sum_{n=1}^{\textup{rk}(E)}c_{n}(E)z^{-n}:=z^{-\text{rk}(E)}\textup{Eu}(E\otimes q)=\prod_{i=1}^{\textup{rk}(E)}(1+\frac{{e}_{i}}{z})

where
{e}_{1},...,{e}_{\text{rk}(E)}\in H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}(Q_{M}),\varphi_{W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}}})
denote the Chern roots of
E
and

\hskip-28.45274pt\textup{Eu}(E\otimes q)=s^{*}s_{*}\ \in{\textup{End}}_{H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A\times\mathbb{C}^{\times}}(\textup{pt})}(H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A\times\mathbb{C}^{\times}}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta},\varphi_{W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}}}))\cong{\textup{End}}_{H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(\textup{pt})}(H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta},,\varphi_{W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}}}))[z]

denotes the
G_{\textbf{d}}\times A\times\mathbb{C}^{\times}
-equivariant Euler class, defined in terms of
s:X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}\to|E\otimes q|
the zero section, where
{\mathbb{C}}^{\times}
acts trivially on
X
,
q
denotes its standard one dimensional, weight one representation, and we identify
H^{\bullet}_{\mathbb{C}^{\times}}(\textup{pt})\cong\mathbb{C}[z]
.

For each
{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q}}
, there are
G_{\textbf{d}}\times A
equivariant tautological bundles
\mathcal{V}^{i}_{\textbf{d}}
on
X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta}
of rank
d_{i}
for each
i\in I_{M}
which define classes in
K_{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta})
, in terms of which we can define the canonical classes
\mathcal{F}_{\textbf{d}}^{i}
by

\mathcal{F}_{\textbf{d}}^{i}=\ _{i}\Sigma\otimes_{S_{M}}\mathcal{V}_{\textbf{d}}=\bigoplus_{j\in I_{M}}\ {}_{i}\Sigma_{j}\otimes\mathcal{V}_{\textbf{d}}^{j}\ \in K_{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta})

for each
i\in I_{M}=V_{Q_{Y}}\cup\{\infty\}
, where we view
\Sigma
with its cohomological and
T
gradings as a complex of representations of
A
.

We now define an action
\mathcal{H}^{0}\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}^{\zeta})
of the universal Cartan algebra
\mathcal{H}^{0}
on
{\mathbb{V}}^{\zeta}
in components

\mathcal{H}^{0}\to{\textup{End}}_{F}(H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta},\varphi_{W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}}})\otimes_{H^{\bullet}_{A}(\textup{pt})}F)\ ,

by the action of the generators
\phi^{i}_{n}
on
{\mathbb{V}}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(M)
, according to the formula

\phi^{i}(z)\mapsto c_{-1/z}(\mathcal{F}_{\textbf{d}}^{i})\ \in{\textup{End}}_{F}(H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta},\varphi_{W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}}})\otimes_{H^{\bullet}_{A}(\textup{pt})}F){[\![}z^{-1}{]\!]}\ ,

for each
i\in V_{Q_{Y}}
.

Recall that the representation structure map
\mathcal{H}\to{\textup{End}}({\mathbb{V}}^{\zeta})
constructed in Theorem
5.6
is defined in terms of the maps

For the remainder of this section, we will in additional assume that the

In particular, there is a natural pairing

.

There exists a natural action right action

]
,

∎

In particular, we define the formal generating functional

f^{i}(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}f^{i}_{n}z^{-n-1}\in\mathcal{SH}^{\textup{op}}[z^{-1}]\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad f_{n}^{i}=(e_{n}^{i})^{\textup{op}}\in\mathcal{SH}^{\textup{op}}\ ,

and note that the induced relations between the generators

Finally, we consider the action by the endomorphisms

\tilde{\psi}^{i,j}_{n,m}=[\rho(e^{i}_{n}),\rho(f^{j}_{m})]\ \in{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}^{\zeta})\ .

We assume that these endomorphisms vanish for

in terms of a rational function

and we call the integer

the shift of the corresponding root

.

We define the shifted Cartan algebra
\mathcal{H}^{0}_{M}
as the polynomial algebra

\mathcal{H}^{0}_{M}=\mathcal{H}^{0}_{M}(Y)=F[\psi_{n}^{i}]_{n\in\mathbb{N}}^{i\in I}\quad\quad\text{and let}\quad\quad\psi^{i}(z)=z^{-s_{i}}+\sum_{n=s_{i}}^{\infty}\psi^{i}_{n}z^{-n-1}\quad\in z^{-s_{i}}\mathcal{H}^{0}{[\![}z^{-1}{]\!]}\

be the corresponding formal generating functional for the variables

. Moreover, we obtain a natural action
\mathcal{H}^{0}_{M}\to{\textup{End}}_{F}(\mathbb{V}^{\zeta})
of the shifted Cartan algebra
\mathcal{H}^{0}_{M}
on

defined in components

(5.17)

\mathcal{H}^{0}_{M}\to{\textup{End}}_{H^{\bullet}_{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(\textup{pt})}(H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}},\zeta},\varphi_{W_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}}})\otimes_{H^{\bullet}_{A}(\textup{pt})}F)\quad\quad\text{by}\quad\quad\psi^{i}(z)\mapsto\tilde{\psi}^{i}(z)=Q^{i}_{M}(z)c_{-1/z}(\mathcal{F}_{\textbf{d}}^{i})\ .

By construction, the relations between the images of the generators
\tilde{e}^{i}_{n}=\rho(e^{i}_{n})
and

under the respective representations are summarized in terms of generating functions as

[\tilde{e}^{i}(z),\tilde{f}^{j}(w)]=\delta_{i,j}\frac{\tilde{\psi}^{i}(z)-\tilde{\psi}^{i}(w)}{z-w}\quad\in{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}^{\zeta}){(\!(}z^{-1}{)\!)}{[\![}w^{-1}{]\!]}\ .

We now recall the definition of (shifted) quiver Yangians given in
[

]
(and

Definition 5.11
.

The
shifted quiver Yangian

\mathcal{Y}_{M}=\mathcal{Y}_{M}(Y)
is the associative algebra over
F
generated by elements

and
\psi^{i}_{m}
for

,

, and

, subject to the relations

(5.18)

\displaystyle\psi^{i}(z)e^{j}(w)

\displaystyle=e^{j}(w)\psi^{i}(z)P^{i}_{j}(z-w)

\displaystyle\in\mathcal{Y}_{M}{(\!(}z^{-1}{)\!)}{[\![}w^{-1}{]\!]}

(5.19)

\displaystyle\psi^{i}(z)f^{j}(w)

\displaystyle=f^{j}(w)\psi^{i}(z)P^{i}_{j}(z-w)^{-1}

\displaystyle\in\mathcal{Y}_{M}{(\!(}z^{-1}{)\!)}{[\![}w^{-1}{]\!]}

(5.20)

\displaystyle[e^{i}(z),f^{j}(w)]

\displaystyle=\delta_{i,j}\frac{\psi^{i}(z)-\psi^{i}(w)}{z-w}

\displaystyle\in\mathcal{Y}_{M}{[\![}z^{-1},w^{-1}{]\!]}

(5.21)

\displaystyle\psi^{i}(z)\psi^{j}(w)

\displaystyle=\psi^{j}(w)\psi^{i}(z)

\displaystyle\in\mathcal{Y}_{M}{[\![}z^{-1},w^{-1}{]\!]}
