\displaystyle e^{i}(z)e^{j}(w)

\displaystyle=e^{j}(w)e^{i}(z)P^{i}_{j}(z-w)

\displaystyle\in\mathcal{Y}_{M}{[\![}z^{-1},w^{-1}{]\!]}

(5.23)

\displaystyle f^{i}(z)f^{j}(w)

\displaystyle=f^{j}(w)f^{i}(z)P^{i}_{j}(z-w)^{-1}

\displaystyle\in\mathcal{Y}_{M}{[\![}z^{-1},w^{-1}{]\!]}

together with the Serre relations between the various
e^{i}_{n}
generators, and similarly between the
f^{i}_{n}
.

Under the above hypotheses, we make the following conjecture:

Conjecture 5.12
.

The maps of Equations
5.11
,
5.14
and
5.17
define a representation

\mathcal{Y}_{M}(Y)\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}^{\zeta}(M)^{A})

of the shifted quiver Yangian
\mathcal{Y}_{M}(Y)
on
\mathbb{V}^{\zeta}(M)^{A}
.

In particular, it is implicit in the conjecture that the restriction of the representation to the positive half
\mathcal{Y}^{+}(Y,M)
agrees with the restriction to the spherical subalgebra
\mathcal{SH}
of the representation of
\mathcal{H}
constructed in Theorem
5.6
, as this is the definition of the representation in Equation
5.11
. In the case
Y=\mathbb{C}^{3}
, the above conjecture holds in the sense that the above construction is equivalent to that of
[
SV13
]
, also obtained in unpublished work of Feigin-Tsymbaliuk recalled in
[
Tsy17
]
, and
[
RSYZ19
]
, although the shift is trivial in all these cases. Several other examples were also explored in
[
RSYZ20
]
in this framework with non-trivial shifts. Moreover, the cohomological analogue of the recent results of
[
Neg23
]
, together with the above construction, appear to imply the above conjecture, but we leave a detailed discussion of this for future work.

6.
Yangians of threefolds and vertex algebras of divisors

6.1.
Perverse coherent systems, Donaldson-Thomas theory, and quiver Yangians

In this section, we let
M=\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]
be the structure sheaf of the threefold
Y
shifted down in cohomological degree by 1. As we observed in Example
4.40
, the extension group
{}_{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}=\Ext^{1}(\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1],\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1])=0
is trivial so that the only possible framing structure for each rank
d_{\infty}={{r}}
is the trivial one
{\textup{f}}_{{r}}=\{0\}
. Moreover, the notion of
\mathcal{F}_{{\textup{f}}_{r}}^{\textup{c}}
-framed perverse coherent extension is closely related to the notion of perverse coherent system, in the sense of
[
NN10
]
, as we explain below.

We begin by recalling the definition of perverse coherent systems from
loc. cit.
:

Definition 6.1
.

A
perverse coherent system
on
Y
is a tuple
(H,W,S)
where
H\in\textup{PervCoh}(Y)
is a perverse coherent sheaf and

s:\mathcal{O}_{Y}\otimes W\to H\ ,

is a map of complexes of quasicoherent sheaves. A perverse coherent system on
Y
is called
compactly supported
if the underlying perverse coherent sheaf
H\in\textup{PervCoh}_{\textup{cs}}(Y)
.

Let
\mathfrak{M}_{\overline{\textup{Per}}_{\textup{cs}}(Y)}
denote the moduli stack of compactly supported perverse coherent systems on
Y
, and note there is a natural decomposition

\mathfrak{M}_{\overline{\textup{Per}}_{\textup{cs}}(Y)}=\bigsqcup_{{{r}}\in\mathbb{N}}\mathfrak{M}_{\overline{\textup{Per}}_{\textup{cs}}(Y)}^{{r}}\ ,

where
\overline{\textup{Per}}_{\textup{cs}}(Y)
denotes the component for which the vector space
W
is of dimension
{{r}}\in\mathbb{N}
.

Recall that we observed in Example
4.40
that the extension group

{}_{\infty}\Sigma_{\infty}^{1}=\Ext^{1}(\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1],\mathcal{O}_{Y}[[1])=0\ ,

so that for each rank
d_{\infty}={{r}}\in\mathbb{N}
there is a unique trivial framing structure
{\textup{f}}_{{r}}=\{0\}
. We can now state the desired equivalence:

Proposition 6.2
.

There is an equivalence of algebraic
\mathbb{K}
stacks

\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}_{{\textup{f}}_{{r}}}^{\textup{cs}}}(Y,\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1])\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathfrak{M}_{\overline{\textup{Per}}_{\textup{cs}}(Y)}^{{r}}\ ,

where we recall that
\mathcal{F}_{{\textup{f}}_{0}}^{\textup{cs}}
is as in Equation
4.39
.

Proof.

By definition, the moduli stack
\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}_{{\textup{f}}_{{r}}}^{\textup{cs}}}(Y,\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1])
parameterizes perverse coherent extensions of
\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]
equipped with an isomorphism of the underlying iterated extension of
\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]
with
\mathcal{O}_{Y}\otimes W[1]
for
W
a vector space of rank
{{r}}
, by Example
4.39
.

Further, recall from Example
4.40
that we observed the extension groups between
\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]
and the simple objects
F_{i}\in\textup{PervCoh}_{\textup{cs}}(Y)
are given by

\ \ {}_{j}\Sigma^{1}_{\infty}=\Ext^{1}(F_{j},\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1])=0\quad\quad_{\infty}\Sigma^{1}_{j}=\Ext^{1}(\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1],F_{j})=\begin{cases}\mathbb{K}&\textup{if $j=0$}\\
\{0\}&\textup{otherwise}\end{cases}\ ,

where the only non-trivial extension class is given by

\mathcal{O}_{C}\to\mathcal{I}_{C}[1]\to\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]\quad\quad\text{induced by}\quad\quad\mathcal{I}_{C}[1]\to\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]\to\mathcal{O}_{C}[1]\ .

Thus, the only possible extensions of
\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]
with the generators
F_{i}
is given by the map
\mathcal{O}_{Y}\to F_{0}
.

Similarly, note that in this case the potential
W_{M}^{{\textup{f}}_{r}}
is independent of the framing arrows, so there is a canonical map of
{\mathbb{K}}
stacks

\mathfrak{M}^{\mathcal{F}_{{\textup{f}}_{{r}}}^{\textup{cs}}}(Y,\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1])\to\mathfrak{M}(Y)\ ,

which corresponds to taking the subobject given by the underlying iterated extension of the generators
F_{i}\in\textup{PervCoh}_{\textup{cs}}(Y)
. For each compactly supported perverse coherent sheaf
H\in\mathfrak{M}(Y)(\mathbb{K})
, the observations above imply that the only possible perverse coherent extension with subobject
H
is given by a map from the underlying iterated extension of
\mathcal{O}_{Y}
, which has a fixed isomorphism with the object
\mathcal{O}_{Y}\otimes W
, to the object
H
. This provides the desired map
s:\mathcal{O}_{Y}\otimes W\to F
.

∎

As a corollary of Proposition
6.2
together with Theorem
4.28
, we obtain that there is a canonical monad presentation for perverse coherent systems, given by that of Example
4.40
. In the case of the resolved conifold studied in
[
Sze08
]
and
[
NN10
]
, the monad presentation is that of Equation
4.43
, though the results also apply in the more general setting studied in
[
Nag12
]
. Indeed, the corresponding framed quivers with potential
(Q_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]}^{{\textup{f}}_{{r}}},W^{{\textup{f}}_{{r}}}_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]})
in this case are precisely those studied in
loc. cit.
.

For each choice of compatible stability condition
\zeta\in\mathbb{R}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}
, the corresponding homology module
\mathbb{V}^{\zeta}_{Y}:=\mathbb{V}^{\zeta}(\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1])
defined in Section
5.4
is given by

(6.1)

\hskip-28.45274pt\mathbb{V}^{\zeta}_{Y}=\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{Y})\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}(Q_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]}^{{\textup{f}}_{{r}}}),\varphi_{W^{{\textup{f}}_{{r}}}_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]}})\otimes_{H^{\bullet}_{A}(\textup{pt})}F\ ,

or equivalently, under the hypotheses of Section
5.5
, which hold in our examples of interest,

\mathbb{V}^{\zeta}_{Y}=\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}H_{\bullet}^{A}(\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}(Q_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]}^{{\textup{f}}_{{r}}}),\varphi_{\overline{W}^{{\textup{f}}_{{r}}}_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]}})\otimes_{H^{\bullet}_{A}(\textup{pt})}F\ .

We also define the corresponding generating functional, as in Equation
5.8
, by

{\mathcal{Z}}_{Y}^{\zeta}({{\textbf{q}}})=\sum_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}{{\textbf{q}}}^{\textbf{d}}\chi(\mathbb{V}^{\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]))\ \in{{\mathbb{Z}[\![{{\textbf{q}}}]\!]}}\ ,

where we recall the shorthand notation
{{\textbf{q}}}^{\textbf{d}}=\prod_{i\in V_{Q_{Y}}}q_{i}^{d_{i}}
and
{{\mathbb{Z}[\![{{\textbf{q}}}]\!]}}=\mathbb{Z}[\![q_{i}]\!]_{i\in V_{Q_{Y}}}
.

The results of
[
NN10
]
and
[
Nag12
]
, in particular Proposition 3.17 and Theorem 3.18 of the latter, imply that for stability conditions
\zeta_{\textup{DT}},\zeta_{\textup{PT}},\zeta_{\textup{NCDT}}
in appropriately chosen chambers, the corresponding homology modules are given by the (categorified) Donaldson-Thomas series
[
DT98
]
, Pandharipande-Thomas series
[
PT09
]
, and non-commutative Donaldson-Thomas series
[
Sze08
]
, that is, we have

{\mathcal{Z}}_{Y}^{\zeta_{\textup{DT}}}={\mathcal{Z}}_{Y}^{\textup{DT}}\quad\quad{\mathcal{Z}}_{Y}^{\zeta_{\textup{PT}}}={\mathcal{Z}}_{Y}^{\textup{PT}}\quad\quad{\mathcal{Z}}_{Y}^{\zeta_{\textup{NCDT}}}={\mathcal{Z}}_{Y}^{\textup{NCDT}}\ ,

where the latter are defined as the generating functions of the corresponding enumerative invariants of the threefold
Y
. In fact, it was proved in
[
NN10
]
using the results of
[
BF08
]
that these invariants can be computed via equivariant localization in terms of signed counts of fixed points, so that we have

{\mathcal{Z}}_{Y}^{\zeta}({{\textbf{q}}})=\sum_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}{{\textbf{q}}}^{\textbf{d}}(-1)^{k_{\textbf{d}}}|\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}(Q_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]}^{{\textup{f}}_{{r}}},W^{{\textup{f}}_{{r}}}_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}[1]})^{A}|\ ,

in keeping with Corollary
5.8
, which was written following
loc. cit.
.

Example 6.3
.

Let
Y=\mathbb{A}^{3}
and
r=1
, so that the framed quiver with potential
(Q^{{\textup{f}}_{1}}_{\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{A}^{3}}},W^{{\textup{f}}_{1}}_{\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{A}^{3}}})
is given by that on the left in Equation
4.42
. It is well known that for a generic stability condition
\zeta
, the corresponding moduli space of
\zeta
-stable representations such that
\dim V_{0}=n
is given by

\mathfrak{M}_{n}^{\zeta}(Q^{{\textup{f}}_{1}}_{\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{A}^{3}}},W^{{\textup{f}}_{1}}_{\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{A}^{3}}})=\textup{Hilb}_{n}(\mathbb{A}^{3})\ ,

the Hilbert scheme of points on
\mathbb{C}^{3}
. The set of
T
-fixed points
{\text{\<p>}}_{n}
of
\textup{Hilb}_{n}(\mathbb{A}^{3})
is labeled by the set of length
n
plane partitions, so that we have

\mathbb{V}_{\mathbb{C}^{3}}^{\zeta}\cong\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\bigoplus_{\lambda\in{\text{\<p>}}_{n}}F_{\lambda}\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad F_{\lambda}=F

is a copy of the base field
F
for each
n\in\mathbb{N}
and
\lambda\in{\text{\<p>}}_{n}
.
Further, the results of
[
BF08
]
in this case imply that the DT series is given by

\mathcal{Z}_{\mathbb{C}^{3}}^{\zeta}(q_{0})=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1-(-q_{0})^{k})^{k}}\quad\in\mathbb{Z}[\![q_{0}]\!]\ .

We also introduce notation for the MacMahon function

M(x,q)=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1-xq^{k})^{k}}\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad M(q)=M(1,q)=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1-q^{k})^{k}}\ ,

so that we can write simply

\mathcal{Z}_{\mathbb{C}^{3}}^{\zeta}(q)=M(q)\quad\quad\text{for}\quad\quad q=-q_{0}\ .

Example 6.4
.

The approach to studying the DT series of more general threefolds via quivers with potential was pioneered by Szendroi in the seminal paper
[
Sze08
]
in the case
Y_{1,1}=|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)^{\oplus 2}|
, and the framed quiver with potential considered in
loc. cit.
is that on the right in Equation
4.42
. In this case, it was conjectured in
loc. cit.
based on extensive computational evidence and proved in
[
You09
]
that the non-commutative DT series of
Y_{1,1}
is given by

\mathcal{Z}^{{\textup{NCDT}}}_{Y_{1,1}}(q_{0},q_{1})=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1+q_{0}^{k}(-q_{1})^{k-1})^{k}(1+q_{0}^{k}(-q_{1})^{k+1})^{k}}{(1-q_{0}^{k}(-q_{1})^{k})^{2k}}\ .

If we let
q=-q_{0}q_{1}
and
x=q_{1}
then this expression can equivalently be written

(6.2)

\mathcal{Z}^{{\textup{NCDT}}}_{Y_{1,1}}(q,x)=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1-x^{-1}q^{k})^{k}(1-xq^{k})^{k}}{(1-q^{k})^{2k}}=M(1,q)^{2}M(x^{-1},q)^{-1}M(x,q)^{-1}\ .

Example 6.5
.

Similar results were obtained in
[
BY10
]
for toric quotient singularities. In particular, for
Y_{2,0}=|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-2)|
with corresponding framed quiver with potential that in the middle of Equation
4.42
, the formula for the non-commutative DT series from
loc. cit.
is given by

(6.3)

\mathcal{Z}^{{\textup{NCDT}}}_{Y_{2,0}}(q,x)=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1-q^{k})^{2k}(1-x^{-1}q^{k})^{k}(1-xq^{k})^{k}}=M(1,q)^{2}M(x^{-1},q)M(x,q)\ ,

where we again let
q=-q_{0}q_{1}
and
x=q_{1}
.

More generally, for
Y_{m,0}=\tilde{A}_{m-1}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}
, the analogous formula from
loc. cit.
is given by

(6.4)

\mathcal{Z}^{{\textup{NCDT}}}_{Y_{m,0}}(q,x_{i})=M(1,q)^{n}\prod_{1\leq a\leq b\leq m-1}M(x_{[a,b]}^{-1},q)M(x_{[a,b]},q)\ ,

where we let
q=-q_{0}q_{1}...q_{m-1}
,
x_{i}=q_{i}
for
i=1,...,m-1
, and
x_{[a,b]}=x_{a}x_{a+1}\ldots x_{b}
.

The cohomological Hall algebra of Kontsevich-Soibelman
[
KS11a
]
was defined so that it naturally acts on the cohomology of DT theory type moduli spaces (see for example the discussion in
[
Soi16
]
and the review
[
Sze15
]
) and in this case the results of Section
5.4
simply reproduce this fact:

Corollary 6.6
.

There exists a natural representation

(6.5)

\rho_{Y}:\mathcal{H}(Y)\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}_{Y}^{\zeta})

of Equation
6.1
is naturally a module for of the cohomological Hall algebra
\mathcal{H}(Y)
on the categorified DT-type series
\mathbb{V}^{\zeta}_{Y}
for each compatible stability condition
\zeta\in\mathbb{R}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}
.

The extension of this action to a larger associative algebra containing
\mathcal{H}(Y)
as a positive subalgebra in some triangular decomposition was widely anticipated in this setting. The basic idea was already present in the original papers of Lusztig
[
Lus91
]
and Ringel
[
Rin90
]
, and was proposed explicitly in the context of cohomological DT theory by Soibelman
[
Soi16
]
(see also Section 7.3 of the review
[
Sze15
]
). Moreover, by the
dimensional reduction
equivalence between the critical and preprojective cohomological Hall algebra in some examples, established in
[
YZ16
]
and the appendix to
[
RS15
]
, the results of
[
Nak00
]
,
[
Var00
]
and more recently
[
SV13
]
and
[
SV17
]
suggested a relationship between
\mathcal{H}(Y_{m,0})
and affine Yangian type quantum groups.

Motivated by related considerations in string theory developed in the series of papers
[
Cos13
]
,
[
Cos16
]
, and
[
Cos17
]
, the following conjecture was formulated by Costello.

Conjecture 6.7
.

[
Cos18
]
Let
Y_{m,n}\to X_{m,n}
be a resolution of the affine, toric, Calabi-Yau singularity
X_{m,n}=\{xy-z^{m}w^{n}\}
. Then there exists a natural representation

\rho:\mathcal{Y}_{-\delta}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}_{Y_{m,n}}^{\zeta_{\textup{NCDT}}})\ ,

of the
-\delta
shifted affine Yangian
\mathcal{Y}_{-\delta}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})
of
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m|n}
on
{\mathbb{V}}_{Y_{m,n}}^{\zeta_{\textup{NCDT}}}
, inducing an isomorphism

\rho(\mathcal{Y}_{-\delta}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})_{+})\xrightarrow{\cong}\rho_{Y_{m,n}}(\mathcal{SH}(Y_{m,n}))\ ,

and such that
{\mathbb{V}}_{Y_{m,n}}^{\zeta_{\textup{NCDT}}}
is identified with the vacuum module
V_{m,n}
for
\mathcal{Y}_{-\delta}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})
.

Our expectation is that the proof of this conjecture will follow from Conjecture
5.12
together with the identification

\mathcal{Y}(Y_{m,n}):=\mathcal{Y}_{\mathcal{O}[1]}(Y_{m,n})\cong\mathcal{Y}_{-\delta}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})

so that the induced isomorphism of the positive half with
\mathcal{SH}
follows by construction

\mathcal{Y}_{-\delta}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})_{+}\cong\mathcal{Y}(Y_{m,n})_{+}:=\mathcal{SH}(Y_{m,n})\ .

Indeed, our understanding is that some form of this conjecture is essentially proved along these lines in
[
LY20
]
and
[
GLY21
]
, and we hope that the present paper will help to develop a more robust translation of their work to the language of geometric representation theory. The conjecture was also checked for
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{1}
in
[
RSYZ20
]
, following several related results, using precisely the approach described here. Indeed, Section
5.6
was was written following
loc. cit.
, as well as the references therein and the many indicated here. Closely related results were also obtained in
[
VV20
]
,
[
Liu21
]
and
[
VV23
]
.

There are also several more conceptual approaches to understanding the appearance of Yangians in this setting, including
[
MO19
]
and
[
DM16
]
. We hope to better understand the results presented here in such terms, but this is not addressed in the present work.

As a consequence of Conjecture
6.7
, we expect equality between the non-commutative DT series of the threefold
Y_{m,n}
and the Poincare
series of the vacuum module
V_{m,n}
for
\mathcal{Y}_{-\delta}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})
:

Corollary 6.8
.

There is a natural grading on
V_{m,n}
such that

\mathcal{Z}_{Y_{m,n}}^{{\textup{NCDT}}}(q)=P_{q}(V_{m,n})\ \in\mathbb{Z}{[\![}q{]\!]}

where
P_{q}\in\mathbb{Z}{[\![}q{]\!]}
denotes the Poincare series.

Indeed, in the case
n=0
, the PBW theorem for the affine Yangian of
{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{n}
proved in
[
Gua07
]
gives a filtration on
\mathcal{Y}(\widehat{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}}_{m})
such that we identifications of the associated graded

\textup{gr}\ \mathcal{Y}(\widehat{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}}_{m})\cong\textup{Sym}^{\bullet}(\widehat{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}}_{m}[u^{\pm},v])\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad\textup{gr}\ \mathcal{Y}_{\delta}(\widehat{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}}_{m})\cong\textup{Sym}^{\bullet}({{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m}[t_{1},t_{2}])\ ,

where
\widehat{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}}_{m}[u^{\pm},v]
denotes the universal central extension of
{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m}[u^{\pm 1},v]
and
{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m}[t_{1},t_{2}]
denotes the subalgebra spanned by polynomials in
t_{1}=u
and
t_{2}=u^{-1}v
with coefficients in
{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m}
, so that the corresponding associated graded of the vacuum module
V_{m,0}^{{\mathfrak{sl}}}
for
{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m}
is given by

\textup{gr}\ V_{m,0}^{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}}\cong\bigotimes_{r=0}^{\infty}\textup{Sym}^{\bullet}(\widehat{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}}_{m}[u^{\pm 1}])\otimes_{\textup{Sym}^{\bullet}(u^{-r}{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}}_{m}[u])}\mathbb{K}\ ,

the Poincare polynomial of which is given by

P_{q}(V_{m,0}^{{\mathfrak{sl}}})=\prod_{r=0}^{\infty}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1-q^{k+r})^{m^{2}-1}}=\left(\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1-q^{k})^{k}}\right)^{m^{2}-1}=M(q)^{m^{2}-1}\ .

Similarly, this implies that in the
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m}
case we have

(6.6)

P_{q}(V_{m,0})=M(1,q)^{m^{2}}\ ,

which evidently matches the formula from Equation
6.4
specialized to
x_{i}=1
. Moreover the additional refinement given by the variables
\{x_{i}\}
agrees with the refinement by the grading on
V_{m,0}
under the Cartan
\mathfrak{h}\subset{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m}
.

More generally, we conjecture that the modules induced by the construction of Theorem
5.6
, and its extension outlined in Section
5.6
, in the case of Example
4.49
leads to a family of modules

{\mathbb{V}}_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}^{\zeta}=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}H^{A}_{\bullet}(\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}(Q_{M}^{{\textup{f}}_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}}),\varphi_{\overline{W}_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}}})\otimes_{H_{A}^{\bullet}(\textup{pt})}F

over the affine Yangian of
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{1}
which were constructed in the closely related setting of modules over the quantum toroidal algebra in
[
FJMM12
]
, where
f_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}
is the framing structure on the extended quiver described in Example
4.49
. Their natural analogue in this setting is the following:

Conjecture 6.9
.

There exists a natural representation

\rho:\mathcal{Y}_{-\delta}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{1})\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}^{\zeta_{\textup{NCDT}}}_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma})

such that
{\mathbb{V}}^{\zeta_{\textup{NCDT}}}_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}
is identified with the cohomological variant of the MacMahon module
\mathcal{M}_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}(u)
constructed in
[
FJMM12
]
.

6.2.
Perverse coherent extensions of divisors, Vafa-Witten theory, and vertex algebras

In this section, we explain the application of our results in the case that
M
is given by the structure sheaf of a divisor. Let
S
be an effective toric Cartier divisor in
Y
,
S^{\textup{red}}
the underlying reduced divisor, and
\mathfrak{D}_{S}
its set of irreducible components, so that we have

S^{\textup{red}}=\bigcup_{d\in\mathfrak{D}_{S}}S_{d}\quad\quad\quad\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathfrak{D}_{S}}\mathcal{O}_{S_{d}}\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad[S]=\sum_{d\in\mathfrak{D}_{S}}r_{d}[S_{d}]

for some multiplicities
r_{d}\in\mathbb{N}
defined for each
d\in\mathfrak{D}_{S}
. Let
Q_{\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1]}
denote the extended quiver corresponding to the object
M=\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1]
and note that the data of a Jordan-Holder filtration on
\mathcal{O}_{S}
with subquotients given by the objects
\mathcal{O}_{S_{d}}
determines a framing structure
{\textup{f}}_{S}
of rank
{{\textbf{r}}}_{S}=(r_{d})_{d\in\mathfrak{D}_{S}}
, where we identify
\mathfrak{D}_{S}
with the set of framing nodes of the extended quiver
Q_{S}
. Thus, we can consider the stack of
{\textup{f}}_{S}
-framed perverse coherent extensions of
\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1]

\mathfrak{M}(Y,S):=\mathfrak{M}^{{\textup{f}}_{S}}(Y,\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1])\quad\quad\text{as well as}\quad\quad\mathfrak{M}^{0}(Y,S):=\mathfrak{M}^{0_{S}}(Y,\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1])\ ,

the stack of trivially framed perverse coherent extensions of
\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1]
of rank
{{\textbf{r}}}_{S}
, and their corresponding framed quivers with potential
(Q^{{\textup{f}}_{S}},W^{{\textup{f}}_{S}})
and
(Q^{0_{S}},W^{0_{S}})
. We have seen in Examples
4.41
to
4.47
that certain stable loci
\mathfrak{M}^{\zeta}(Y,S)
or
\mathfrak{M}^{0,\zeta}(Y,S)
in these stacks provide models in algebraic geometry for moduli spaces of framed instantons on
S^{\textup{red}}
of rank
{{\textbf{r}}}_{S}
, that is, of rank
r_{d}
on the irreducible component
S_{d}
for each
d\in\mathfrak{D}_{S}
. Indeed, this gives the desired generalization of the ADHM construction described in Section
1.1
of the introduction.

In particular, in the case
Y={\mathbb{C}}^{3}
and
S=S_{r_{1},r_{2},r_{3}}=r_{1}[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}_{yz}]+r_{2}[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}_{xz}]+r_{3}[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}_{yz}]
, applying Theorem
4.38
as in Example
4.42
implies the desired description in algebraic geometry of the stack
\mathfrak{M}_{\textup{Nek}}^{r_{1},r_{2},r_{3}}({\mathbb{C}}^{3})
of rank
{{\textbf{r}}}=(r_{1},r_{2},r_{3})
representations of the spiked instantons quiver with potential studied in
[
NP17
]
:

Theorem 6.10
.

There is an equivalence of algebraic stacks

\mathfrak{M}_{\textup{Nek}}^{r_{1},r_{2},r_{3}}({\mathbb{C}}^{3})\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathfrak{M}^{0}(\mathbb{C}^{3},S_{r_{1},r_{2},r_{3}})\ .

Similarly, the special cases of this construction in Examples
4.43
,
4.47
, and
4.46
give ‘three dimensional’ variants of the corresponding cases of constructions of
[
KN90
]
,
[
NY08a
]
, and
[
FR10
]
, respectively, analogous to the spiked instantons variant of the ADHM construction. In general, in the case
Y=Y_{m,0}
, this construction conjecturally gives the analogous variant of the relationship between rank
m
, parabolic torsion free sheaves on
\mathbb{P}^{1}\times\mathbb{P}^{1}
and chainsaw quivers from
loc. cit.
. For divisors
S
in the spaces
Y_{m,n}
, we obtain a generalization of this variant of their construction to
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m|n}
. We discuss examples of this form in detail following Conjecture
6.27
below, and in the succeeding Section
6.3
.

For each choice of compatible stability condition
\zeta\in\mathbb{R}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}
, the corresponding homology module
\mathbb{V}_{S}=\mathbb{V}^{{\textup{f}}_{S},\zeta}(Y,\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1])
defines a model for a rank
{{\textbf{r}}}_{S}
cohomological Vafa-Witten type series of
S^{\textup{red}}
, given by

(6.7)

\mathbb{V}_{S}^{\zeta}=\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{Y})\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}(Q^{{\textup{f}}_{S}}),\varphi_{W^{{\textup{f}}_{S}}})\otimes_{H_{A}^{\bullet}(\textup{pt})}F\ ,

or equivalently, again under the hypotheses of Section
5.5
which hold in our examples of interest,

\mathbb{V}_{S}^{\zeta}=\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}H_{\bullet}^{A}(\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta}(Q^{{\textup{f}}_{S}}),\varphi_{\overline{W}^{{\textup{f}}_{S}}})\otimes_{H_{A}^{\bullet}(\textup{pt})}F\ .

We also define the corresponding generating functional, as in Equation
5.8
, by

{\mathcal{Z}}_{S}^{\zeta}({{\textbf{q}}})=\sum_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}{{\textbf{q}}}^{\textbf{d}}\chi(\mathbb{V}^{{\textup{f}}_{S},\zeta}_{\textbf{d}}(\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1]))\ \in{{\mathbb{Z}[\![{{\textbf{q}}}]\!]}}\ ,

where we recall the shorthand notation
{{\textbf{q}}}^{\textbf{d}}=\prod_{i\in V_{Q_{Y}}}q_{i}^{d_{i}}
and
{{\mathbb{Z}[\![{{\textbf{q}}}]\!]}}=\mathbb{Z}[\![q_{i}]\!]_{i\in V_{Q_{s}Y}}
. In particular, we define

{\mathbb{V}}_{S}={\mathbb{V}}^{{\textup{f}}_{S},\zeta_{\textup{VW}}}(\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1])\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad{\mathcal{Z}}_{S}^{{\textup{VW}}}({{\textbf{q}}})=\sum_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}{{\textbf{q}}}^{\textbf{d}}\chi(\mathbb{V}_{S,{\textbf{d}}}))\ \in{{\mathbb{Z}[\![{{\textbf{q}}}]\!]}}\ ,

for
\zeta=\zeta_{\textup{VW}}
the Vafa-Witten stability condition, as well as

{\mathbb{V}}^{0}_{S}={\mathbb{V}}^{0_{S},\zeta}(\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1])\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad\mathcal{Z}_{S}^{0,\zeta}({{\textbf{q}}})=\sum_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}{{\textbf{q}}}^{\textbf{d}}\chi(\mathbb{V}^{0}_{S,{\textbf{d}}}))\ \in{{\mathbb{Z}[\![{{\textbf{q}}}]\!]}}\ ,

corresponding to the trivial framing structure
0_{S}
of rank
{{\textbf{r}}}_{S}
.

Note that again the hypotheses necessary to calculate the generating functional in terms of fixed point counts as in Corollary
5.8
will hold in the main examples of interest, as we will use below:

Example 6.11
.

Let
Y={\mathbb{C}}^{3}
and
S^{\textup{red}}=\mathbb{C}^{2}_{xy}
as in Example
4.41
. For
S=S^{\textup{red}}
and generic
\zeta
, the moduli space of
\zeta
-stable, trivially-framed perverse coherent extensions of
M=\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1]
of rank 1 and dimension
{\textbf{d}}=n
corresponds under dimensional reduction to the Hilbert scheme of
n
points on
\mathbb{C}^{2}
, so that we have

(6.8)

{\mathbb{V}}_{{\mathbb{C}}^{2}}=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}H_{\bullet}^{A}(\textup{Hilb}_{n}(\mathbb{C}^{2}))\otimes_{H^{\bullet}_{A}(\textup{pt})}F\cong\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\bigoplus_{\lambda\in{\text{\<p>}}_{n}}F_{\lambda}\

where
{\text{\<p>}}_{n}
denotes the set of
A
-fixed points of
\textup{Hilb}_{n}(\mathbb{C}^{2})
, which is in bijection with the set of partitions
\lambda
of length
n
, and
F_{\lambda}
denotes a copy of the field of fractions of
H_{A}^{\bullet}(\textup{pt})
. It follows that the corresponding generating function is given by

(6.9)

\mathcal{Z}_{{\mathbb{C}}^{2}}^{\textup{VW}}(q)=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{1-q^{k}}=\eta(q)^{-1}\ .

More generally, for
S=r[\mathbb{C}^{2}]
the module for the trivial framing
{\textup{f}}=0
is given by

(6.10)

\mathbb{V}_{r[\mathbb{C}^{2}]}^{0}\cong\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}H_{\bullet}^{A}(M(r,n))\otimes_{H^{\bullet}_{A}(\textup{pt})}F\cong\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\bigoplus_{n_{1}+\ldots+n_{r}=n}\bigotimes_{j=1}^{r}H_{\bullet}^{A}(\textup{Hilb}_{n_{j}})\otimes_{H^{\bullet}_{A}(\textup{pt})}F\cong\bigotimes_{j=1}^{r}{\mathbb{V}}_{{\mathbb{C}}^{2}}

and thus the generating function for the trivially framed extensions is given by that for
r
-tuples of partitions of total length
n
:

(6.11)

\mathcal{Z}^{0}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]}(q)=\prod_{j=1}^{r}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{1-q^{k}}=\eta(q)^{-r}\ .

For
{\textup{f}}={\textup{f}}_{S}
, again following Example
4.41
, the fixed points of the moduli spaces are restricted from arbitrary
r
-tuples of partitions to
nested partitions
, those which satisfy the additional requirement that each partition is a strict subset of the previous; this was studied in
[
CCDS21
]
in precisely this setting and our examples of this form were inspired by their work.

Under the identification

\mathbb{V}_{r[\mathbb{C}^{2}]}^{0}\cong\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\bigoplus_{n_{1}+\ldots+n_{r}=n}\bigotimes_{j=1}^{r}\left(\bigoplus_{\lambda_{j}\in{\text{\<p>}}_{n_{j}}}F_{\lambda_{j}}\right)\cong\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\bigoplus_{n_{1}+\ldots+n_{r}=n}\bigoplus_{\lambda_{1},\ldots,\lambda_{r};\lambda_{j}\in{\text{\<p>}}_{n_{j}}}F_{\lambda_{1},...,\lambda_{r}}

the module
{\mathbb{V}}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]}
is given by the submodule

(6.12)

\mathbb{V}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]}\cong\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\bigoplus_{n_{1}+\ldots+n_{r}=n}\bigoplus_{\lambda_{1}\geq\ldots\geq\lambda_{r};\lambda_{j}\in{\text{\<p>}}_{n_{j}}}F_{\lambda_{j}}\quad\quad\text{and thus}\quad\quad\mathcal{Z}^{\textup{VW}}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]}(q)=\prod_{j=1}^{r}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{1-q^{j+k}}\ .

Example 6.12
.

For
Y={\mathbb{C}}^{3}
and
S=S_{M,N,0}=M[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}_{xy}]+N[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}_{yz}]
, as in the special case of Example
4.42
corresponding to the quiver in Equation
4.49
, we expect that the set of
A
fixed points of
\mathcal{M}(Y,S)
is in bijection with the set of plane partitions with a pit at location
(M,N)
and trivial asymptotics, in the sense of
[
BFM15
]
.

Example 6.13
.

More generally, let
Y={\mathbb{C}}^{3}
,
S=S_{M,N,0}=M[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}_{xy}]+N[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}_{yz}]
and

M=\mathcal{O}_{S^{\textup{red}}}^{\textup{ss}}[1]\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}_{x}}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{y}}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{z}}\ ,

following Example
4.50
, with the framing structure given by that described in
loc. cit.
, and we expect the fixed points of the resulting moduli space to correspond to plane partitions with a pit at location
(M,N)
and asymptotics
\alpha,\beta,\gamma
determined as in
loc. cit.
. A special case of the resulting family of quivers is given by the quiver of Equation
4.70
.

Example 6.14
.

Let
Y=|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)|
and
S=|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)|
as in Example
4.47
. The vanishing cycles cohomology defining
{\mathbb{V}}_{S}
is equivalent to the ordinary Borel-Moore homology of the dimensional reduction, and thus by localization we have an isomorphism

(6.13)

{\mathbb{V}}_{|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)|}\cong\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\bigoplus_{n_{0}+n_{1}=n}\bigoplus_{\lambda_{0}\in{\text{\<p>}}_{n_{0}},\lambda_{1}\in{\text{\<p>}}_{n_{1}}}F_{k,\lambda_{0},\lambda_{1}}

by Proposition 3.2 and Theorem 3.4 in
[
NY05
]
, where
{\text{\<p>}}_{n}
denotes the set of partitions of
n
.

Similarly, Corollary 5.7 of
[
NY08b
]
applied in the limit
m=\infty
to each term
k=c_{1}\in\mathbb{Z}
, the partition function is given by the following formula of Corollary 3.15 in
[
NY03
]

(6.14)

\mathcal{Z}^{\textup{VW}}_{|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)|}(q)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}q^{\frac{k^{2}}{2}}\frac{1}{\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}(1-q^{k})^{2}}\ .

The representation of the cohomological Hall algebra
\mathcal{H}(Y)
on
{\mathbb{V}}_{S}
constructed in Theorem
5.6
, and its extension to the action of the shifted quiver Yangian
\mathcal{Y}_{M}(Y)
outlined in Section
5.6
, were essentially defined to generalize the construction of Grojnowski
[
Gro96
]
and Nakajima
[
Nak97
]
of the Heisenberg algebra action on the Hilbert scheme of points, following the Schiffmann-Vasserot proof
[
SV13
]
of the AGT conjecture
[
AGT10
]
and their respective generalizations in
[
RSYZ19
]
and
[
GR19
]
. We note that these results are also closely related to those obtained in unpublished work of Feigin-Tsymbaliuk, as explained in
[
Tsy17
]
, and in turn to many results in the setting of quantum toroidal algebras such as
[
FFJ+11
]
and
[
BFM15
]
; we will elaborate on this relationship further in Section
6.3
below.

The proposal that there should be analogous vertex algebras corresponding to more general divisors
S
and threefolds
Y
was considered already in the original paper of Gaiotto-Rapcak
[
GR19
]
, and explored in some detail in
[
PR18
]
, but the analogue of the AGT conjecture in this setting was not known in general, as the relevant moduli spaces generalizing the spiked instantons construction of Nekrasov to threefolds
Y
other than
{\mathbb{C}}^{3}
had not been constructed previously.

There is also a closely related conjecture of Feigin-Gukov
[
FG20
]
that there should exist vertex operator algebras
\text{VOA}[M_{4},{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r}]
associated to four manifolds
M_{4}
, analogously generalizing the AGT conjecture. This appears to coincide with the predictions of
[
GR19
]
discussed in the preceding paragraph in the case that the underlying reduced scheme
S^{\textup{red}}
is irreducible and smooth,
M_{4}
is the analytification of
S^{\textup{red}}
, and
r\in\mathbb{N}
the multiplicity of
S^{\textup{red}}
in
S
.

However, a mathematical definition of these vertex algebras was also not known in general, for a divisor
S
nor four-manifold
M_{4}
, and relatively few examples were known in the non-abelian case. In the companion paper
[
But23
]
, we give a general combinatorial construction of vertex algebras
{\mathbb{V}}(Y,S)
as the kernel of screening operators acting on lattice vertex algebras determined by the data of the GKM graph of
Y
and a Jordan-Holder filtration of
\mathcal{O}_{S}
with subquotients structure sheaves
\mathcal{O}_{S_{d}}
of the divisors
S_{d}
occurring as irreducible, reduced components of
S
. This construction appears to satisfy the predictions of
[
GR19
]
,
[
PR18
]
, and
[
FG20
]
, and in particular we formulate the following analogue of the AGT conjecture in this setting:

Conjecture 6.15
.

There exists a natural representation

\rho:\mathcal{U}({\mathbb{V}}(Y,S))\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}_{S})

of the algebra of modes
\mathcal{U}({\mathbb{V}}(Y,S))
of the vertex algebra
{\mathbb{V}}(Y,S)
on
{\mathbb{V}}_{S}
, inducing an isomorphism

\rho(\mathcal{U}({\mathbb{V}}(Y,S))_{+})\xrightarrow{\cong}\rho_{S}(\mathcal{SH}(Y))

and such that
{\mathbb{V}}_{S}
is identified with the vacuum module for the vertex algebra
{\mathbb{V}}(Y,S)
.

While we are not currently able to give a proof in general, note that the conjectural identification with the action of
\mathcal{SH}(Y)
implies that Theorem
5.6
together with Proposition
5.10
provide the desired construction of the action of the algebra of modes. We expect that the proof will follow from the compatibility between the free field realizations of
{\mathbb{V}}(Y,S)
used in their construction in
[
But23
]
, and a family of coproducts on the corresponding shifted quiver Yangians
\mathcal{Y}_{S}(Y)
, under equivalences of the type conjectured in the following Section
6.3
. We hope to explore this further in future work.

As a consequence of Conjecture
6.15
, we expect equality between the Vafa-Witten-type series
\mathcal{Z}^{\textup{VW}}_{S}(q)
of the divisor
S
defined above and the Poincare series
P_{q}
of the vacuum module
{\mathbb{V}}_{(Y,S)}
of the vertex algebra
{\mathbb{V}}(Y,S)
.

Corollary 6.16
.

There is a natural grading on
{\mathbb{V}}_{(Y,S)}
such that

\mathcal{Z}^{\textup{VW}}_{S}(q)=P_{q}({\mathbb{V}}_{(Y,S)})\ \in\mathbb{Z}{[\![}q{]\!]}\ .

Indeed, the above conjecture and corollary can be verified directly in several of the simplest examples, following the previous work on the subject mentioned above:

Example 6.17
.

In the case
Y={\mathbb{C}}^{3}
and
S={\mathbb{C}}^{2}
, the constructions we have outlined reduce to the original constructions of Grojnowski
[
Gro96
]
and Nakajima
[
Nak97
]
. The vertex algebra

{\mathbb{V}}({\mathbb{C}}^{3},{\mathbb{C}}^{2})=\pi_{k}

is simply the Heisenberg algebra
\pi_{k}
at level
k=-\frac{1}{\hbar_{1}\hbar_{2}}
, the module
{\mathbb{V}}_{{\mathbb{C}}^{2}}
of Equation
6.8
is evidently isomorphic to the standard Fock module, and the vacuum character is given by
\eta(q)^{-1}
, which is indeed the Vafa-Witten-type series for
{\mathbb{C}}^{2}
of Equation
6.9
above.

Example 6.18
.

More generally, the constructions of
loc. cit.
generalize to smooth surfaces
S
to give the Heisenberg algebra
\pi(S)
on the cohomology
H_{A}^{\bullet}(S;{\mathbb{C}})
over the base field
F
; we have included
A
-equivariance following
[
Nak99b
]
in keeping with our present setting. Thus, the vacuum module of
\pi(S)
is given by

\pi_{S}\cong\textup{Sym}_{F}^{\bullet}(z^{-1}(H^{A}_{\bullet}(S)\otimes_{H_{A}^{\bullet}(\textup{pt})}F)[z^{-1}])\quad\quad\text{so that}\quad\quad P_{q}(\pi_{S})=\eta(q)^{-\chi(S)}\ ,

by the formula of
[
Göt90
]
. Indeed, we show in
[
But23
]
that the Heisenberg algebra
\pi(S)
canonically embeds in the vertex algebra
{\mathbb{V}}(Y,S)
, but for
H_{2}(S;\mathbb{Z})\neq 0
it is a strict subalgebra.

In fact, we explain in
loc. cit.
that in the rank 1 case, corresponding to our assumption that
S
is a smooth algebraic surface and in particular reduced when considered as a divisor, the vertex algebra
{\mathbb{V}}(Y,S)
is simply the lattice vertex algebra generated by
H_{2}(S;\mathbb{Z})
equipped with negative the intersection pairing, tensored with the Heisenberg algebra generated by
H_{0}(S)
,

\mathbb{V}(Y,S)=V_{H_{2}(S;\mathbb{Z})}\otimes\pi_{H^{0}(S;{\mathbb{C}})}\ .

The additional generators of the lattice vertex algebra correspond to the Hecke modifications of the sheaves along the compact curve classes in
H_{2}(S;\mathbb{Z})
, as in the construction outlined in the final chapter of
[
Nak99a
]
. This is also related to the results of
[
Nak94
]
and
[
GKV95
]
.

We note that the construction of Negut
[
Neg17
]
provides a higher rank analogue of the construction of Grojnowski-Nakajima, generalizing Example
6.20
below to more general surfaces
S
, but the resulting vertex algebras analogously fail to include the lattice-type extensions corresponding to Hecke modifications along curve classes, which our construction conjecturally provides.

Example 6.19
.

As a special case of the preceding Example
6.18
, let
Y=|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)|
and
S=|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)|
following Examples
6.14
and in turn
4.47
. Indeed, we have an isomorphism between the vacuum module of Equation
6.13
and that of a canonically normalized rank 1 lattice vertex algebra
V_{\mathbb{Z}}
tensored with a Heisenberg algebra,

\mathbb{V}_{|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)|}\cong V_{\mathbb{Z}}\otimes\pi\quad\quad\text{and in particular}\quad\quad P_{q}(V_{\mathbb{Z}}\otimes\pi)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}q^{\frac{k^{2}}{2}}\frac{1}{\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}(1-q^{k})^{2}}=\mathcal{Z}^{\textup{VW}}_{|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)|}(q)\ ,

we obtain equality of the Poincare polynomial of the vacuum module with the Vafa-Witten type series of
|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)|
given in Equation
6.14
. Moreover, we have checked by direct calculation that the conjecture holds following our proposed construction in this example, using results of
[
NY05
]
,
[
NY08a
]
,
[
NY08b
]
; this result will appear in future work.

Example 6.20
.

For
Y={\mathbb{C}}^{3}
and
S=r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]
, as in Example
6.11
, the definition of the vertex algebra
{\mathbb{V}}(Y,S)
from
[
But23
]
is simply the Feigin-Frenkel free field realization of the principal affine
W
-algebra of
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r}
, so that we have

{\mathbb{V}}({\mathbb{C}}^{3},r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}])=W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r})\cong W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{r})\otimes\pi\ ,

where we use the notation
W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r})
to denote the vertex algebra over the field of fractions of
H_{\tilde{T}}^{\bullet}(\textup{pt})
defined by

\kappa=-h^{\vee}-\frac{\hbar_{2}}{\hbar_{1}}\ .

In this case, our proposed construction was defined to reproduce that of
[
SV13
]
used in the proof of the AGT conjecture
[
AGT10
]
, and moreover the variant thereof studied in
[
CCDS21
]
which produces the vacuum module, as in the statement of Conjecture
6.15
. In
[
SV13
]
the authors prove the following theorem:

Theorem 6.21
.

[
SV13
]
There exists a natural representation

\mathcal{U}(W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r}))\to{\textup{End}}({\mathbb{V}}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]}^{0})\ ,

such that
{\mathbb{V}}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]}^{0}
is identified with the universal Verma module
\mathbb{M}_{r}
for
W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r})
.

In
[
CCDS21
]
, the authors extend these results to give a geometric construction of the vacuum module as the cohomology of the moduli space of stable representations of a variant of the ADHM construction, for which the quiver is precisely that corresponding to taking
A_{\textup{f}}
equal to a principal nilpotent in Equation
4.44
of Example
4.41
. Thus, in the notation we have introduced, they prove:

Theorem 6.22
.

[
CCDS21
]
There exists a natural representation

\mathcal{U}(W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r}))\to{\textup{End}}({\mathbb{V}}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]})\ ,

such that
{\mathbb{V}}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]}
is identified with the vacuum module for
W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r})
.

In particular, we have the identification

P_{q}(W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r}))=\prod_{j=1}^{r}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{1-q^{k+j}}=\mathcal{Z}^{\textup{VW}}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]}(q)\ ,

as desired, where we recall that
{\mathbb{V}}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]}
and
\mathcal{Z}^{\textup{VW}}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]}(q)
are given by the expressions of Equation
6.12
, and we have used the usual abuse of notation denoting the vacuum module by the underlying vertex algebra
W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r})
.

These results are also closely related to the cohomological variant of
[
FFJ+11
]
, as well as
[
BFM15
]
in the case
n=0
. In particular, note that the fixed point counting underlying the decomposition of
{\mathbb{V}}_{r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]}
in Equation
6.12
is precisely that considered in
loc. cit.
.

Example 6.23
.

More generally, for
Y={\mathbb{C}}^{3}
and
S=S_{M,N,0}=M[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}_{xy}]+N[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}_{yz}]
as in Example
6.12
, the vertex algebras
{\mathbb{V}}({\mathbb{C}}^{3},S_{M,N,0})
are the Gaiotto-Rapcak
Y
algebras
Y_{N,0,M}
of
[
GR19
]
, and the construction from
[
But23
]
reduces to their definition in
[
RSYZ19
]
. Moreover,
loc. cit.
established the variant of Conjecture
6.15
proved in
[
SV13
]
, related to the Verma module rather than the vacuum, for
Y={\mathbb{C}}^{3}
and arbitrary
S_{M,N,L}
. Their construction was a significant source of inspiration for the results of this paper. Analogous results were also established in the setting of quantum toroidal algebras for
L=0
in
[
BFM15
]
.

Following Example
6.12
, the corresponding quivers are given by the special case of Example
4.42
in Equation
4.49
, with
A_{3}^{2}=A_{2}^{3}=0
and
A_{2},A_{3}
principal nilpotents in
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M}
and
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{N}
, respectively, and the fixed points are in correspondence with the plane partitions with a pit at location
(M,N)
of
[
BFM15
]
, with trivial asymptotics
\alpha=\beta=\gamma=\O
.

More generally, in analogy with Conjecture
6.9
, we expect that the modules induced by the construction of Theorem
5.6
in the case of Example
6.13
where
S=S_{M,N,0}=M[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}_{xy}]+N[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}_{yz}]
define certain canonical families of modules

{\mathbb{V}}_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}^{M,N}=\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}H_{\bullet}^{A}(\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}}_{S;\alpha,\beta,\gamma},\zeta_{\textup{VW}}}(Q_{M}),\varphi_{\overline{W}_{M,{\textbf{d}}}^{{\textup{f}}_{S;\alpha,\beta,\gamma}}})\otimes_{H_{A}^{\bullet}(\textup{pt})}F

over the vertex algebras
{\mathbb{V}}({\mathbb{C}}^{3},S_{M,N,0})
, with fixed point bases enumerated by plane partitions with a pit and fixed asymptotics as in
[
BFM15
]
, determined by the framing structure
{\textup{f}}_{S;\alpha,\beta,\gamma}
as in Example
4.50
. In particular, we make the following conjecture:

Conjecture 6.24
.

There exists a natural representation

\rho:\mathcal{U}({\mathbb{V}}({\mathbb{C}}^{3};S_{M,N,0}))\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}_{\alpha,\beta,\O}^{M,N})

of the algebra
\mathcal{U}({\mathbb{V}}({\mathbb{C}}^{3};S_{M,N,0}))
on
{\mathbb{V}}_{S;\alpha,\beta,\O}
, identifying it with the module
\mathcal{N}_{\alpha,\beta,\O}^{M,N}
of
loc. cit.
.

We now describe some applications of our results to examples of divisors
S
in a resolution
Y_{m,n}
of
X_{m,n}=\{xy-z^{m}w^{n}\}
. Let
\mu
and
\nu
be partitions of length
m
and
n
, respectively

\mu=\{\mu_{1}\geq\ldots\geq\mu_{m}\geq 0\}\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad\nu=\{\nu_{1}\geq\ldots\geq\nu_{n}\geq 0\}

and define the corresponding lists of integers

\textbf{M}=(M_{i})_{i=0}^{m-1}\quad\textbf{N}=(N_{i})_{i=0}^{n-1}\quad\quad\text{where}\quad\quad M_{i}=\sum_{k=i+1}^{m}\mu_{k}\quad N_{i}=\sum_{k=i+1}^{n}\nu_{k}

i=0,...,m-1
,
j=0,...,n-1
; we also write just

M=M_{0}=\sum_{k=1}^{m}\mu_{k}\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad N=N_{0}=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\nu_{k}\ .

We define
S_{\mu,\nu}
as the toric divisor corresponding to the labeling of the faces of the moment polytope of
Y_{m,n}
by the integers
M_{i}
and
N_{i}
depicted in Figure
1
below in the case
m=3,n=2
. We also write simply
S_{\mu}
or
S_{\nu}
if
n=0
or
m=0
, respectively.

.
The resolution
Y_{3,2}
, the toric divisor
S_{\mu,\nu}
, and the compact toric curve classes
C_{i}
with their corresponding simple roots
\alpha_{i}
of
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{3|2}

In this setting, following physical predictions from
[
PR18
]
we conjecture in
[
But23
]
that the corresponding vertex algebra is given by the affine
W
algebra of
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M|N}
corresponding to the nilpotents
f_{\mu}
and
f_{\nu}
in
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M}
and
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{N}
, respectively, determined by
\mu
and
\nu
:

Conjecture 6.25
.

[
But23
]
There is an isomorphism of vertex algebras

W_{f_{\mu},f_{\nu}}^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M|N})\xrightarrow{\cong}{\mathbb{V}}(Y_{m,n},S_{\mu,\nu})\ .

In fact, we have a proof of this conjecture in the case
n=0
, which will appear in future work:

Theorem 6.26
.

There is an isomorphism of vertex algebras

W^{\kappa}_{f_{\mu}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M})\xrightarrow{\cong}{\mathbb{V}}(Y_{m,0},S_{\mu})\ .

The quivers that arise in this setting are generalizations of the variant of the
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{2}
chainsaw quiver considered in Example
4.46
, and in general we conjecture there exists an appropriate framing structure and dimensional reduction relating the resulting module with the ordinary Borel-Moore homology of the moduli space of representations of the corresponding chainsaw quiver. We now formally state this conjecture:

Let
\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\mu}(Q^{\textup{Ch}}_{m},W^{\textup{Ch}}_{m})
denote the stack of
d
dimensional representations of the
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m}
chainsaw quiver as in
[
FR10
]
, with fixed framing dimension given by the integers
\mu_{i}
, so that following the conjectures of Kanno-Tachikawa
[
KT11
]
and in turn
[
Bra04
]
, we expect that

(6.15)

\mathbb{M}_{f_{\mu}}\xrightarrow{\cong}\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}H^{A}_{\bullet}(\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\mu,\zeta}(Q^{\textup{Ch}}_{m},I^{\textup{Ch}}_{m}))\otimes_{H_{A}^{\bullet}(\textup{pt})}F\ ,

the
A
-equivariant Borel-Moore homology of the moduli space of stable representations of the
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m}
chainsaw quiver
(Q^{\textup{Ch}}_{m},I^{\textup{Ch}}_{m})
of framing dimension
\mu
is identified with the universal Verma module
\mathbb{M}_{f_{\mu}}
for the affine W-algebra
W_{f_{\mu}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M})
associated to the nilpotent
f_{\mu}
in
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M}
.

Let
{\textup{f}}_{0}
be the framing structure for
S_{\mu}
of rank
M
generalizing that of Equation
4.59
, that is, such that the map
V_{\infty_{i}}\to V_{\infty_{i-1}}
is injective for each
i=1,...,m-1
and all other framing endomorphisms are zero. We denote the corresponding module by

{\mathbb{V}}_{S_{\mu}}^{{\textup{f}}_{0}}=\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}H_{\bullet}^{A}(\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}}_{0},\zeta_{\textup{VW}}}(Y_{m,0},S_{\mu}),\varphi_{\overline{W}^{{\textup{f}}_{0}}})\otimes_{H_{A}^{\bullet}(\textup{pt})}F\ .

Following the equivalence outlined at the end of Example
4.46
, we make the following conjecture:

Conjecture 6.27
.

There is a canonical isomorphism

H_{\bullet}^{A}(\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{{\textup{f}}_{0},\zeta}(Y_{m,0},S_{\mu}),\varphi_{\overline{W}^{{\textup{f}}_{0}}})\cong H^{A}_{\bullet}(\mathfrak{M}_{\textbf{d}}^{\mu,\zeta}(Q^{\textup{Ch}}_{m},I^{\textup{Ch}}_{m}))\ .

As explained in
loc. cit.
, the expectation is that this follows from dimensional reduction, in the sense of Theorem A.1 of
[
Dav17
]
, for example, together with an equivalence given by passing to cokernels of the injective maps determined by the framing structure. In particular, note that the dimensions of the framing vector spaces in the two quiver descriptions of the above equivalence differ in the following way:
\mathfrak{M}^{f_{0},\zeta}(Y_{m,0},S_{\mu})
parameterizes representations of framing dimension
M
while
\mathfrak{M}^{\mu,\zeta}(Q^{\textup{Ch}}_{m},I^{\textup{Ch}}_{m})
parameterizes representations of framing dimension
\mu
, noting that

\mu_{i}=M_{i-1}-M_{i}\ .

This is the generalization of the relation outlined between the framing vector spaces
V_{\infty_{0}}
and
\tilde{V}_{\infty_{0}}
in the quivers of Equations
4.58
and
4.59
, respectively.

In summary, we expect that the preceding Conjecture
6.27
together with an identification of the form in Equation
6.15
imply that the module constructed by the framing structure
{\textup{f}}_{0}
above is identified with the universal Verma module
\mathbb{M}_{f_{\mu}}
of the corresponding
W
-algebra:

Conjecture 6.28
.

There exists a natural representation

\mathcal{U}(W_{f_{\mu}}^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M}))\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}_{S_{\mu}}^{{\textup{f}}_{0}})\ ,

such that
{\mathbb{V}}_{S_{\mu}}^{{\textup{f}}_{0}}
is identified with the universal Verma module
\mathbb{M}_{f_{\mu}}
.

The preceding equivalence is the analogue of Theorem
6.21
recalled from
[
SV13
]
, and is closely related to several existing mathematical generalizations of the AGT conjecture, such as
[
BFFR11
]
,
[
FFNR11
]
,
[
Neg18
]
,
[
Neg20
]
, and
[
CDM23
]
. However, we have not considered the modules corresponding to the framing structures that feature in Conjecture
6.15
. Indeed, the framing structure
{\textup{f}}_{S_{\mu}}
can be described by adding to
{\textup{f}}_{0}
an additional principal nilpotent
G_{\textup{f}}
in
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M_{0}}
acting at the framing vertex corresponding to
{\mathbb{C}}^{2}
; the modification of the framed quiver with potential in Equation
4.58
, which corresponds to the framing structure
{\textup{f}}_{0}
, is depicted in Figure
2
above:

\end{overpic}

.
The toric divisor
S_{\mu}
in
Y_{2,0}
and framed quiver with potential
(Q^{{\textup{f}}_{S_{\mu}}},W^{{\textup{f}}_{S_{\mu}}})

We recall that the module associated to the divisor
S
which features in Conjecture
6.15
in defined in terms of the corresponding quiver with potential as

{\mathbb{V}}_{S_{\mu}}={\mathbb{V}}_{S_{\mu}}^{{\textup{f}}_{S_{\mu}},\zeta_{\textup{VW}}}=\bigoplus_{{\textbf{d}}\in\mathbb{N}^{V_{Q_{Y}}}}H_{\bullet}^{G_{\textbf{d}}(Q_{Y})\times A}(X_{\textbf{d}}^{\zeta_{\textup{VW}}}(Q^{{\textup{f}}_{S_{\mu}}}),\varphi_{W^{{\textup{f}}_{S_{\mu}}}})\otimes_{H_{A}^{\bullet}(\textup{pt})}F\ .

The statement of
loc. cit.
in this setting, by Theorem
6.26
, gives the following conjecture:

Conjecture 6.29
.

There exists a natural representation

\mathcal{U}(W_{f_{\mu}}^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M}))\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}_{S_{\mu}})\ ,

such that
{\mathbb{V}}_{S_{\mu}}
is identified with the vacuum module
W_{f_{\mu}}^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M})
.

More generally, following Conjecture
6.25
, we make the analogous conjectures in the
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m|n}
case:

Conjecture 6.30
.

There exists a natural representations

\mathcal{U}(W_{f_{\mu},f_{\nu}}^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M|N}))\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}_{S_{\mu,\nu}}^{0})\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad\mathcal{U}(W_{f_{\mu},f_{\nu}}^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M|N}))\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}_{S_{\mu,\nu}})\ ,

such that
{\mathbb{V}}_{S_{\mu,\nu}}^{0}
and
{\mathbb{V}}_{S_{\mu,\nu}}
are identified with the verma and vacuum modules of
W_{f_{\mu},f_{\nu}}^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M|N})
.

6.3.
Towards isomorphisms between
W
-superalgebras and Yangians for
\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_{m|n}

As at the end of the preceding section, let
Y_{m,n}\to X_{m,n}
be a resolution of the affine, toric, Calabi-Yau singularity
X_{m,n}=\{xy-z^{m}w^{n}\}
. In this section, we explain the analogue of Conjecture
6.7
for
{\mathbb{V}}_{S}
, the module constructed from a divisor
S
in
Y_{m,n}
in the preceding section, and moreover explain its expected relationship with Conjecture
6.15
. This gives a geometric approach to prove a variant of the main theorem of
[
BK04
]
: an isomorphism between affine
W
-superalgebras and truncated shifted Yangians of
{{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n}
.

To begin, recall from Proposition
3.1
that

\textup{Pic}(\hat{Y})\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathbb{\mathbb{Z}}^{I_{+}}\quad\quad\text{by}\quad\quad\mathcal{L}\mapsto\deg\iota_{i}^{*}\mathcal{L}

where
I_{+}
is the index set of the irreducible components
C_{i}
of the fibre
C
of the resolution over the
T
-fixed point
x\in X
, and
\iota_{i}:C_{i}\to Y
are their the inclusions. For
Y=Y_{m,n}
, we thus have identifications of the Picard group of
\hat{Y}_{m,n}
with the root lattice of
{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m|n}
and the index set
I_{+}
with the set of positive simple roots for
{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m|n}
,

\textup{Pic}(\hat{Y}_{m,n})\cong Q_{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m|n}}\quad\quad\text{and}\quad\quad I_{+}\cong\Pi_{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m|n}}\ .

For example, in Figure
1
we have depicted the four compact toric curve classes
C_{i}
in
Y_{3,2}
and the corresponding positive simple roots
\alpha_{i}
in
{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m|n}
.

Following
[
BK04
]
, the shifted Yangian is defined in terms of a square matrix
\sigma
of size
|\Pi|+1
called the
shift matrix
, which is uniquely determined by its entries
s_{i,i+1}
and
s_{i+1,i}
immediately above and below the diagonal, for
i=1,...,|\Pi|
. Now, given a divisor
S
in
Y_{m,n}
, we define the corresponding shifts of real roots as the intersection numbers

s_{i+1,i}=\langle[C_{i}],S\rangle\quad\quad\text{for}\quad\quad i=1,...,|\Pi_{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{m|n}}|=m+n-1

where we have assumed for simplicity that all these numbers are non-negative, as will be the case for
S_{\mu,\nu}
as long as
\mu_{m}\geq\nu_{1}
. We let
\sigma_{S}
denote the induced shift matrix, and
\mathcal{Y}_{\sigma_{S}}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})
the corresponding shifted Yangian of
{{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n}
with respect to the shift of real roots determined by
\sigma_{S}
; for example, the divisor
S_{\mu,\nu}
in
Y_{3,2}
from the example of Figure
1
induces the shift matrix given by

\sigma_{S_{\mu,\nu}}=\left[\begin{array}[]{c c c | c c}0&0&0&0&0\\
\mu_{1}-\mu_{2}&0&0&0&0\\
\mu_{1}-\mu_{3}&\mu_{2}-\mu_{3}&0&0&0\\
\hline\cr\mu_{1}-\nu_{1}&\mu_{2}-\nu_{1}&\mu_{3}-\nu_{1}&0&0\\
\mu_{1}-\nu_{2}&\mu_{2}-\nu_{2}&\mu_{3}-\nu_{2}&\nu_{1}-\nu_{2}&0\end{array}\right]\ .

We can now state the analogue of the Conjecture
6.7
of Costello
[
Cos18
]
for the modules
{\mathbb{V}}_{S}
corresponding to divisors
S
in
Y_{m,n}
:

Conjecture 6.31
.

There exists a natural representation

\rho:\mathcal{Y}_{\sigma_{S}}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}_{S})\ ,

of the
\sigma_{S}
shifted affine Yangian
\mathcal{Y}_{\sigma_{S}}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})
of
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m|n}
on
\mathbb{V}_{S}
, inducing an isomorphism

\rho(\mathcal{Y}_{\sigma_{S}}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})_{+})\xrightarrow{\cong}\rho_{S}(\mathcal{SH}(Y_{m,n}))\ .

As for Conjecture
6.7
, we expect that the proof of the preceding conjecture will follow from Conjecture
5.12
together with an identification

\mathcal{Y}_{S}(Y_{m,n}):=\mathcal{Y}_{\mathcal{O}_{S}[1]}(Y_{m,n})\cong\mathcal{Y}_{\sigma_{S}}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})\ .

In fact, for general
Y
and
S
, we expect that this action factors as a surjection

\mathcal{Y}_{S}(Y)\to\mathcal{U}({\mathbb{V}}(Y,S))\ ,

or a map with dense image though we will ignore this subtlety in what follows, composed with the representation
\mathcal{U}({\mathbb{V}}(Y,S))\to{\textup{End}}_{F}({\mathbb{V}}_{S})
of Conjecture
6.15
. In particular, we conjecture that for
Y=Y_{m,n}
and
S=S_{\mu,\nu}
this induces a surjection

(6.16)

\mathcal{Y}_{\sigma_{S_{\mu,\nu}}}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})\to\mathcal{U}({\mathbb{V}}(Y_{m,n},S_{\mu,\nu}))

with kernel given by the
\ell^{th}
-truncation ideal for
\ell=\mu_{1}
, so that we have

\mathcal{Y}_{\sigma_{S_{\mu,\nu}}}^{\ell}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathcal{U}({\mathbb{V}}(Y_{m,n},S_{\mu,\nu}))\ .

In summary, together with Conjecture
6.25
, we obtain:

Conjecture 6.32
.

There is a canonical isomorphism

(6.17)

\mathcal{Y}_{\sigma_{S_{\mu,\nu}}}^{\ell}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathcal{U}(W_{f_{\mu},f_{\nu}}^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M|N}))\ ,

where
\mu,\nu
are the unique dominant coweights such that
\sigma=\sigma_{S_{\mu,\nu}}
and
\ell=\mu_{1}
.

This is precisely the analogue for
{{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n}
of the main theorem of
[
BK04
]
, which was originally proved for the Yangian of
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{N}
. Some results along these lines have been obtained recently in
[
Ued20
]
,
[
Neg22
]
and
[
KU21
]
in the case
\sigma=0
and
\mu
and
\nu
are given by rectangular partitions, but the statement of the conjecture for general shift appears to be new. There is also an example in the non-rectangular case given in
[
Ued22
]
, but given the apparent absence of a shift of real roots in this result, we are unsure whether the map constructed in
loc. cit.
has an analogous geometric origin.

We also propose the existence of a natural limiting vertex algebra, generalizing the usual
W_{1+\infty}
algebra, as follows: let
\sigma
be a shift matrix for
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m|n}
and let
\mu^{1},\nu^{1}
be the minimal in the dominance order among the coweights corresponding to
\sigma
as in Conjecture
6.32
, or equivalently those such that
\ell^{1}=\mu^{0}_{1}
is minimal, where we have assumed
\mu_{n}\geq\nu_{1}
for simplicity. More generally, let
\mu^{r}
and
\nu^{r}
denote the
{r}^{th}
smallest coweights corresponding to
\sigma
, and let
M_{r}=|\mu^{r}|
and
N_{r}=|\nu^{r}|
. Then we propose to consider the large
r
limit algebra, conjecturally enhanced to include
r
as a parameter,

W^{\kappa}_{1+\infty,\sigma}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m|n}):=\ \text{``}\ \lim_{{r}\to\infty}W^{\kappa}_{f_{\mu^{r}},f_{\nu^{r}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M_{r},N_{r}})\ \text{''}\ ,

which defines a
\sigma-
shifted variant of the
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m|n}
-extended
W_{1+\infty}
vertex algebra, which was introduced in
[
Cos16
]
for
n=0
, and studied further and generalized to
n\neq 0
in
[
EGR18
]
,
[
CH18
]
,
[
EP19
]
,
[
CHU19
]
and
[
Rap19
]
. In terms of this vertex algebra, the preceding conjecture implies the following, which has an interpretation in string theory as an example of the twisted holographic principle of Costello-Li
[
CL16
]
for M5 branes in the
\Omega
-background, following the approach of
[
Cos16
]
:

Conjecture 6.33
.

There is a canonical isomorphism of associative algebras

\mathcal{Y}_{\sigma}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n})\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathcal{U}(W^{\kappa}_{1+\infty,\sigma}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m|n}))\ ,

inducing isomorphisms as in Equation
6.17
for each compatible
l\in\mathbb{N}
,
\mu
,
\nu
, and an identification

V_{m,n;\sigma}\xrightarrow{\cong}W^{\kappa}_{1+\infty,\sigma}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m|n})

between the vacuum module
V_{m,n;\sigma}
of the
\sigma
-shifted affine Yangian of
{{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{m|n}
and that of
W^{\kappa}_{1+\infty,\sigma}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m|n})
.

We hope to provide a proof of this conjecture in future work, using the geometric approach developed here. In what follows, we explain the conjecture in the case of
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{1}
for which it follows from
[
SV13
]
, and provide some numerical evidence for the general statement. In particular, we note the following corollary of the preceding conjecture, which we verify holds in the examples below:

Corollary 6.34
.

Let
\sigma
be a shift matrix for
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{m|n}
, and for each
{r}\in\mathbb{N}
let
\mu^{r}
and
\nu^{r}
be the dominant coweights defined as above. Then

(6.18)

P_{q}(V_{m,n;\sigma})=\lim_{{r}\to\infty}P_{q}(W^{\kappa}_{f_{\mu^{r}},f_{\nu^{r}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M^{r}|N^{r}}))\ .

Note that the choice of shift matrix
\sigma
together with
{r}\in\mathbb{N}
determines not only the dominant coweights
\mu^{r}
and
\nu^{r}
but an enhancement of them to a
pyramid
, in the sense of
[
EK03
]
. This determines a good grading with respect to which we define
W^{\kappa}_{f_{\mu^{r}},f_{\nu^{r}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{M^{r},N^{r}})
and the Poincare polynomial on the right hand side of Equation
6.18
.

We now proceed to the discussion of examples:

Example 6.35
.

Let
m=1
and
n=0
so that
Y=Y_{1,0}={\mathbb{C}}^{3}
. In this case, there are no real roots with which to shift the Yangian, and the isomorphism

\mathcal{Y}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{1})\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathcal{U}(W_{1+\infty}^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{1}))

was explained in
[
GGLP17
]
, following the proof of the AGT conjecture from
[
SV13
]
and the unpublished results of Feigin-Tsymbaliuk explained in
[
Tsy17
]
. Moreover, the results of
[
SV13
]
and their generalizations in
[
RSYZ19
]
, which we recall establish special cases of Conjecture
6.15
as outlined in Examples
6.20
and
6.23
, respectively, also prove the special cases of Conjecture
6.31
in these examples. Further, in these cases, the proofs of the two conjectures are related precisely as described in the discussion following
loc. cit.
.

In particular, for each
r\in\mathbb{N}
we can compute the Poincare polynomial of the vacuum module of
{\mathbb{V}}({\mathbb{C}}^{3},r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}])=W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r})
following the spectral sequence argument from Section 15.2.9 of
[
FBZ04
]
, as we recall below; this is summarized in Figure
3
.

Figure 3
.
The divisor
r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]
in
{\mathbb{C}}^{3}
, with associated pyramid
\pi
, induced grading
\Gamma
, and Poincare polynomial
P_{q}
of the vacuum module of
W_{f_{\textup{prin}}}^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{{r}})

The computation of
loc. cit.
proceeds as follows: given the divisor
S=r[{\mathbb{C}}^{2}]
, consider the corresponding pyramid
\pi
as explained above, the grading
\Gamma
induced by
\pi
, and compute the degree with respect to
\Gamma
of the highest weights of each of the irreducible representations occurring in the decomposition of the adjoint of
{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r}
under the
{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{2}
embedding, representatives of which are written in bold in Figure
4
. Each such highest weight can be lifted to a field of
W^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r})
of the corresponding conformal weight, and it is proved in
loc. cit.
that these fields form a set of strong generators, in terms of which we can compute the Poincare polynomial of the vacuum module, usually called the
character
of the vertex algebra.

In general, the character of
W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r})
computed as outlined above is given by

P_{q}(W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r}))=\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{1-q^{j+k}}

and we find a direct verification of Corollary
6.34
above

\lim_{r\to\infty}P_{q}(W^{\kappa}_{f_{\textup{prin}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r}))=\lim_{r\to\infty}\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{1-q^{j+k}}=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1-q^{k})^{k}}=M(q)=P_{q}(V_{1,0})\ ,

where we have used the equality of Equation
6.6
above in the case
m=1
.

.

Let
m=2
and
n=0
, so that
Y=Y_{2,0}\to X_{2,0}=\{xy-z^{2}\}\times\mathbb{C}
. The corresponding lattice of real roots is given by
\textup{Pic}(\hat{Y}_{2,0})\cong Q_{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{2}}\cong\mathbb{Z}
, and to begin we suppose the shift is trivial, that is
\sigma=\scriptsize{\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\
0&0\end{bmatrix}}
. For each
r\in\mathbb{N}
, there is a dominant coweight
\mu^{r}
corresponding to
\sigma
determined as above, and the corresponding divisor
S_{\mu^{r}}
is pictured on the left of Figure
4
below. Moreover, the corresponding pyramid
\pi
and good grading
\Gamma
, together with the character of the vacuum module for the
W
-algebra

determined by this grading, are pictured on the right.

Figure 4
.
The toric divisor
S_{\mu^{r}}
in
Y_{2,0}
for
\sigma=\scriptsize{\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\
0&0\end{bmatrix}}
, with associated pyramid
\pi
, induced grading
\Gamma
, and Poincare polynomial
P_{q}
of the vacuum module of
W_{f_{\mu^{r}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{2{r}})

For example, for
r=1
the coweight
\mu^{1}
corresponds to the trivial nilpotent
f_{\mu^{1}}=0
, so that the corresponding
W
-algebra is the affine Kac-Moody algebra
V^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{2})
, and the conjectural map
\mathcal{Y}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{2})\to\mathcal{U}(V^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{2}))\cong\mathcal{U}({{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}}_{2})
of Equation
6.16
is simply the evaluation homomorphism constructed in
[
Gua07
]
. The vertex algebra
V^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{2})
is strongly generated by a collection of fields of conformal weight 1 enumerated by any basis of the underlying Lie algebra, and thus the character of the vacuum module is given by
\eta(q)^{-4}
. Evidently this agrees with the
r=1
case of the general formula

P_{q}(W_{f_{\mu^{r}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{2r}))=\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1-q^{k+j})^{4}}\ ,

from Figure
4
. Moreover, we can again verify Corollary
6.34
directly in this case:

\lim_{r\to\infty}P_{q}(W_{f_{\mu^{r}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{2r}))=\lim_{r\to\infty}\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1-q^{k+j})^{4}}=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1-q^{k})^{4k}}=M(q)^{4}=P_{q}(V_{2,0})\ ,

where again we have used the equality of Equation
6.6
.

Example 6.37
.

Let
m=2
and
n=0
, so that
Y=Y_{2,0}\to X_{2,0}=\{xy-z^{2}\}\times\mathbb{C}
, as in the preceding example, and suppose the shift matrix is given by
\sigma_{1}=\scriptsize{\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\
1&0\end{bmatrix}}
. Again, the sequence of toric divisors, and their corresponding pyramids, good gradings, and vacuum module characters are pictures in Figure
5
below.

For example, in the case
r=2
the coweight
\mu^{2}
corresponds to the subregular nilpotent
f_{\mu^{2}}\in{{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{3}
, so that the corresponding vertex algebra is given by the Bershadsky-Polyakov
W_{3}^{(2)}
algebra, the subregular
W
-algebra for
{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{3}
, tensored with a Heisenberg algebra. It is well known that the
W_{3}^{(2)}
vertex algebra is strongly generated by four fields
J,L,G^{+}
and
G^{-}
of conformal weights
1
,
2
,
\frac{3}{2}
and
\frac{3}{2}
, respectively.

Figure 5
.
The toric divisor
S_{\mu^{r}}
in
Y_{2,0}
for
\sigma=\scriptsize{\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\
1&0\end{bmatrix}}
, with associated pyramid
\pi
, induced grading
\Gamma
, and Poincare polynomial
P_{q}
of the vacuum module of
W_{f_{\mu^{r}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{2{r}-1})

In fact, the traditional conformal weights for the Bershadsky-Polyakov algebra correspond to the Dynkin grading on
W_{f_{\mu^{2}}}({{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{3})
, while with respect to the good grading induced by the pyramid above, the fields
G^{+}
and
G^{-}
are of degree
1
and
2
. Thus, including the auxiliary Heisenberg generator, the character of
{\mathbb{V}}(Y_{2,0},S_{\mu^{2}})=W_{f_{\mu^{2}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{3})
is given by

P_{q}(W_{f_{\mu^{2}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{3}))=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1-q^{k})^{3}(1-q^{k+1})^{2}}\ ,

in agreement with the general formula given in Figure
5
above.

We can again verify Corollary
6.34
directly in this case:

\lim_{r\to\infty}P_{q}(W_{f_{\mu^{r}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{2r-1}))=\lim_{r\to\infty}\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1-q^{k})(1-q^{k+(r-1)})^{2}}{(1-q^{k+j})^{4}}=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1-q^{k})}{(1-q^{k})^{4k}}=P_{q}(V_{2,0;\sigma_{1}})\ .

Example 6.38
.

Let
m=2
and
n=0
, so that
Y=Y_{2,0}\to X_{2,0}=\{xy-z^{2}\}\times\mathbb{C}
, as in the preceding two examples, and suppose now that the shift matrix is given by
\sigma_{2}=\scriptsize{\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\
2&0\end{bmatrix}}
. The sequence of toric divisors, and their corresponding pyramids, good gradings, and vacuum module characters are pictures in Figure
6
below.

We can yet again verify Corollary
6.34
directly in this case:

\displaystyle\lim_{r\to\infty}P_{q}(W_{f_{\mu^{r}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{2r-1}))

\displaystyle=\lim_{r\to\infty}\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1-q^{k})(1-q^{k+1})(1-q^{k+(r-1)})^{2}}{(1-q^{k+j})^{4}(1-q^{k+r})^{2}}

\displaystyle=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1-q^{k})(1-q^{k+1})}{(1-q^{k})^{4k}}=P_{q}(V_{2,0;\sigma_{2}})\ .

Example 6.39
.

Let
m=n=1
so that
Y_{1,1}=|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-1)|\to X_{1,1}=\{xy-zw\}
, so that the lattice of real (super) roots is given by
\textup{Pic}(Y_{1,1})\cong Q_{{{\mathfrak{sl}}}_{1|1}}\cong\mathbb{Z}
, and we consider the case that the shift is trivial, so that
\sigma=\scriptsize{\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\
0&0\end{bmatrix}}
.

As in Example
6.36
, in the unshifted case with
r=1
the corresponding
W
-algebra is the affine Kac-Moody vertex superalgebra
V^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{1|1})
, which is strongly generated by two odd and two even fields all of conformal weight
1
, so that the character of the vacuum module is given by

P_{q}(V^{\kappa}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{1|1}))=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1+q^{k})^{2}}{(1-q^{k})^{2}}\ .

More generally, the vacuum character of the rectangular
W
-superalgebra which corresponds to the divisor
S_{\mu^{r},\nu^{r}}
via Conjecture
6.30
is computed analogously, as summarized in Figure
7
:

P_{q}(W_{f_{\mu^{r}},f_{\nu^{r}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r|r}))=\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1+q^{k+j})^{2}}{(1-q^{k+j})^{2}}\ .

Again, we can verify Corollary
6.34
directly in this case:

\lim_{r\to\infty}P_{q}(W_{f_{\mu^{r}},f_{\nu^{r}}}({{\mathfrak{gl}}}_{r|r}))=\lim_{r\to\infty}\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1+q^{k+j})^{2}}{(1-q^{k+j})^{2}}\\
=\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1+q^{k})^{2k}}{(1-q^{k})^{2k}}=P_{q}(V_{1|1})\ \ ,

in agreement with the computations of the character of the
\mathcal{N}=2
superconformal
W_{1+\infty}
algebras studied in
[
GLP18
]
and
[
GLPZ18
]
. More generally, the analogous computations to those of Examples
6.37
and
6.38
can evidently be checked similarly for divisors on
Y_{1|1}
with non-trivial shift.
